# innostes UI - Complete Documentation

Generated for AI assistants and offline reference.

---

## Accessibility Statement (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/accessibility)

WCAG 2.2 Level AA conformance, component guarantees, developer responsibilities, and assistive technology testing.

`@innostes/ui` is committed to delivering accessible software for all enterprise operators. Every component in the library is built and tested to conform to the **Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 Level AA** standard.

Whether an operator at Northwind Traders Pvt Ltd navigates via keyboard shortcuts, relies on screen readers (such as NVDA or VoiceOver), uses voice control, or enables high-contrast display modes, all workflows must remain fully functional and efficient.

## Conformance target

The design system targets **WCAG 2.2 Level AA** across all four principles:

1. **Perceivable**: Text and graphical elements satisfy minimum contrast ratios (≥ 4.5:1 for normal text, ≥ 3.0:1 for large text and UI components). Visual status is never communicated solely through colour.
2. **Operable**: All interactive elements are reachable and operable via standard keyboard sequences. Focus order matches reading order, focus indicators are clearly visible, and modal overlays trap focus securely without keyboard traps.
3. **Understandable**: Controls provide predictable state updates, clear textual error associations via `aria-describedby`, and consistent interaction patterns across forms and dialogs.
4. **Resilient**: Components rely on semantic HTML5 primitives and WAI-ARIA 1.2 specifications, ensuring compatibility across modern browsers and assistive technologies.

## What the library guarantees

When you use `@innostes/ui` primitives, the library automatically handles:

- **Focus trapping and restoration**: Dialogs, sheets, and alert modals trap keyboard focus within the container and restore focus to the triggering element upon dismissal.
- **Roving tabindex**: Multi-item composite widgets (such as `Tabs`, `RadioGroup`, `DropdownMenu`, `TreeView`, and `ToggleGroup`) manage `tabIndex={0}` and `tabIndex={-1}` automatically, enabling direct arrow-key navigation.
- **ARIA attributes and live regions**: Tooltips, progress bars, toasts, and alerts emit proper ARIA roles (`role="alert"`, `role="status"`, `aria-live="polite"`).
- **Verified token contrast**: Base design tokens in `theme.css` and `dark.css` are validated at build time to satisfy WCAG AA contrast minimums.
- **Motion reduction**: Animations automatically disable or simplify when the user enables `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.

## What the application team must do

Accessibility is a shared responsibility between the library and the consuming application. Application developers must ensure:

| Developer responsibility | Correct implementation | Why it matters |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Labels for icon-only buttons** | `<Button size="icon" aria-label="Delete order PO-881">` | Screen readers cannot interpret SVG glyphs without accessible names |
| **Form error linkage** | Use `<Field>` and `<FieldError>` | Associates error text programmatically with inputs via `aria-describedby` |
| **Heading hierarchy** | Use logical `<h1>` to `<h6>` levels | Screen reader users browse pages by jumping across heading structures |
| **Colour redundancy** | Pair warning badges with an icon | Red-green colour-blind operators cannot rely solely on hue shifts |
| **Table column headers** | Provide `<th>` headers with `scope="col"` | Allows screen readers to announce column context when traversing cells |
| **Alternative text** | Provide descriptive `alt` text on images | Screen readers announce image context for visual assets |

## Testing methods

Our quality assurance pipeline tests accessibility through multiple layers of verification:

1. **Automated component audits**: Unit tests run `axe-core` assertions across component render states to detect missing ARIA attributes, orphan labels, or invalid roles before code merges.
2. **Deterministic contrast validation**: A build-time check (`landing:docs-check`) parses all theme tokens and calculates relative luminance to prevent contrast regressions.
3. **Automated browser crawl**: A Playwright crawler audits documentation pages and interactive showcases for focusability, keyboard loops, and landmark semantics.
4. **Manual assistive technology testing**: Regular manual testing verifies auditory announcements and keyboard flows.

## Assistive technology testing matrix

We test `@innostes/ui` against the following screen-reader and browser pairings:

| Screen reader | Operating system | Tested browsers | Conformance status |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **VoiceOver** | macOS (Sequoia / Sonoma) | Safari, Google Chrome | Fully verified in continuous QA |
| **NVDA** | Windows 11 | Mozilla Firefox, Google Chrome | Fully verified in continuous QA |
| **TalkBack** | Android 14 | Chrome Mobile | Verified for mobile ERP layouts |
| **JAWS** | Windows 11 | Edge, Chrome | Scheduled on enterprise roadmap |
| **Orca** | Linux (Ubuntu / Debian) | Firefox | Scheduled on enterprise roadmap |

## Known issues and continuous hardening

We maintain an active audit tracker (`AUDIT.md`) documenting accessibility improvements:

- **LIB-003**: Customisable internationalisation strings across all ERP widgets (`DataTable`, `TreeView`, `KanbanBoard`) to eliminate hardcoded English text.
- **LIB-004**: Token contrast adjustments across light and dark mode tokens to ensure 100% WCAG AA compliance across all semantic pairings.
- **LIB-007**: Migration from physical directional CSS classes to logical bidirectional properties (`inset-inline-start`, `margin-inline-end`) for full RTL language accessibility.

## Reporting an accessibility problem

If you discover an accessibility barrier or an unannounced state in any `@innostes/ui` component:

1. Open an issue on our repository describing the component, the expected vs actual behaviour, and the assistive technology used (including version numbers).
2. Or contact our accessibility working group directly at `accessibility@innostes.com`.
3. Critical accessibility defects affecting production applications are prioritised as S1 bugs in accordance with our governance policy.

---

## Cartesian Charts (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/charts/cartesian)

Bar, Line, and Area charts for visualizing categorical data series.

Charts live in a **separate entry point** (`@innostes/ui/charts`) to ensure that applications not utilizing charts do not incur the bundle size cost of Recharts.

## Installation

Charts are built on top of [Recharts](https://recharts.org/). You must install it as a peer dependency alongside `@innostes/ui`.

**Important Version Guidance:**
Due to a transitive peer dependency conflict, you must match the Recharts version to your React version:
- **React 17:** Use Recharts **2.15.x** (`pnpm add recharts@^2.15.0`)
- **React 18 / 19:** Use Recharts **3.x** (`pnpm add recharts@^3.0.0`)

```bash
# For React 18 / 19
pnpm add recharts@^3.0.0

# For React 17
pnpm add recharts@^2.15.0
```

## Import

Explicitly import chart components from `@innostes/ui/charts`, **not** from `@innostes/ui` directly.

```tsx
import { BarChart, LineChart, AreaChart } from '@innostes/ui/charts';
```

## Accessibility

A core differentiator of our chart components is their built-in accessibility. Every chart renders an accessible, visually-hidden `<table>` alongside the visual SVG representation (via the internal `ChartFrame` wrapper).

This means screen reader users are not presented with an opaque graphic. Instead, they can navigate the actual tabular data using standard table commands, providing a significantly superior, first-class experience for assistive technology. The `aria-label` prop you provide is used to name this hidden table.

## Props Overview

- **`data`**: An array of objects representing your dataset.
- **`categoryKey`**: The key in your data objects that represents the categories along the X-axis (e.g., `'month'`, `'quarter'`).
- **`series`**: An array of objects defining which keys from the data to plot, shaped as `{ key: string, label: string }`. The `label` is used in legends and tooltips.
- **`valueFormatter`**: An optional function to format the numeric values (e.g., adding currency symbols) for tooltips and axes.
- **`locale`**: Passed to handle localization formatting within the accessible table and tooltips.
- **`aria-label`**: Required string to name the underlying hidden data table for screen readers.

## Theming & Interactions

Colors are automatically assigned from the `chart-1` to `chart-8` categorical tokens defined in `theme.css` and `dark.css`. You can also override colors per series using these tokens or semantic tones (e.g., `success`, `destructive`).

Legends are fully interactive out-of-the-box. Clicking a legend entry toggles the visibility of that data series. If a chart contains only a single series, the legend is automatically hidden to save space and reduce clutter.

## Bar Chart

<ComponentPreview name="charts/cartesian/bar" />

## Line Chart

<ComponentPreview name="charts/cartesian/line" />

## Area Chart

<ComponentPreview name="charts/cartesian/area" />

## API

<ApiTable components={['BarChart', 'LineChart', 'AreaChart']} />

## Donut Chart (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/charts/donut)

A Donut chart for visualizing proportions with a prominent center metric.

Charts live in a **separate entry point** (`@innostes/ui/charts`) to ensure that applications not utilizing charts do not incur the bundle size cost of Recharts.

## Installation

As with all charts, `DonutChart` requires Recharts as a peer dependency.

**Important Version Guidance:**
- **React 17:** Use Recharts **2.15.x** (`pnpm add recharts@^2.15.0`)
- **React 18 / 19:** Use Recharts **3.x** (`pnpm add recharts@^3.0.0`)

## Import

Explicitly import chart components from `@innostes/ui/charts`, **not** from `@innostes/ui` directly.

```tsx
import { DonutChart } from '@innostes/ui/charts';
```

## Accessibility

Just like Cartesian charts, the `DonutChart` automatically renders an accessible, visually-hidden `<table>` containing the raw data and percentage shares. This allows screen readers to navigate the data easily. The `aria-label` prop is required and is used to name this hidden table.

## Center Metric

The `DonutChart` supports a distinct API for displaying a prominent metric in the center of the ring via the `centerValue` and `centerLabel` props. This is ideal for highlighting the primary takeaway of the chart (e.g., total volume, overall percentage).

## Props Overview

- **`data`**: An array of slices to render, each defined as `{ key: string, label: string, value: number, color?: ChartColor }`.
- **`valueFormatter`**: Optional function to format the values displayed in tooltips and the accessible table.
- **`locale`**: Optional locale string for number formatting in the accessible table.
- **`aria-label`**: Required string to name the underlying hidden data table.

## Theming

Slices can be colored automatically using the `chart-1` to `chart-8` categorical tokens, or you can assign specific semantic tones like `success`, `destructive`, or `warning` to individual slices via the `color` property in the data objects.

## Usage

<ComponentPreview name="charts/donut/basic" />

## API

<ApiTable components={['DonutChart']} />

## Charts (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/charts/index)

Accessible, theme-aware charting primitives for financial summaries and inventory analytics.

import { CategoryGrid } from '@/components/docs/category-grid';

# Charts

Chart components deliver accessible, responsive data visualisations across Northwind Traders Pvt Ltd's executive dashboards and operational reports. Built on Recharts with semantic design tokens, they adapt automatically to light and dark themes.

## Components

<CategoryGrid category="charts" />

## Usage guidelines

- **Semantic colour assignment**: Use token-based palette colours rather than hardcoded hex codes to guarantee contrast in both light and dark themes.
- **Data alternatives**: Always provide accessible data tables or summary text alongside charts to ensure full accessibility for screen reader operators.
- **Formatters**: Use localized number and currency formatters (`Intl.NumberFormat`) for tooltip and axis ticks.

## Button Group (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/actions/button-group)

Segmented container joining adjacent buttons horizontally or vertically for pagers and split actions.

ButtonGroup organizes a collection of related button triggers into a cohesive segmented bar, collapsing adjacent borders and rounding only the outer corners. It is commonly used for date pagination controls, multi-part save buttons, and table view switchers.

<ComponentPreview name="actions/button-group/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import { Button, ButtonGroup } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

- **Use ButtonGroup** when grouping related triggers such as pagination controls (Previous / Today / Next) or split action menus (Save / More options).
- **Use ToggleGroup** when buttons toggle pressed states or select mutually exclusive options.
- **Use FormActions** when laying out separate form submission buttons (e.g. Save and Cancel) across a footer.

## Examples

### Basic usage

Wrap adjacent buttons with `ButtonGroup` and assign an accessible label:

```tsx
<ButtonGroup aria-label="Order pagination">
  <Button variant="outline" size="sm">Previous</Button>
  <Button variant="outline" size="sm">Next</Button>
</ButtonGroup>
```

### Split button

Combine a primary action trigger with a contextual dropdown menu button:

```tsx
<ButtonGroup aria-label="Invoice settlement actions">
  <Button variant="primary">Approve and remit</Button>
  <Button
    variant="primary"
    iconOnly
    aria-label="Additional remittance options"
    className="border-s border-s-primary-foreground/20"
  >
    <ChevronDown className="size-4" />
  </Button>
</ButtonGroup>
```

### Orientation

Arrange buttons vertically when building sidebar toolbars:

```tsx
<ButtonGroup orientation="vertical" aria-label="Document view tools">
  <Button variant="outline" size="sm">Zoom in</Button>
  <Button variant="outline" size="sm">Zoom out</Button>
  <Button variant="outline" size="sm">Reset</Button>
</ButtonGroup>
```

## Accessibility

### Keyboard navigation

<KeyboardTable
  rows={[
    { key: 'Tab', action: 'Moves focus sequentially between the individual buttons inside the group.' },
    { key: 'Enter / Space', action: 'Activates the currently focused button.' },
  ]}
/>

### Screen readers and ARIA

- **`role="group"`**: Automatically applied to the wrapper container.
- **`aria-label` requirement**: You **must** provide `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` describing the collection of buttons (e.g. `aria-label="Pagination controls"`).
- **Z-index focus stacking**: Focus rings are rendered with elevated z-index so the active button outline is never clipped by neighbouring buttons.

## Guidelines

<DoDont>
  <Do>
    Always provide an `aria-label` on `ButtonGroup` explaining the shared purpose of the grouped actions.
  </Do>
  <Dont>
    Never use `ButtonGroup` for mutually exclusive selection; use `ToggleGroup` or `RadioGroup` instead.
  </Dont>
</DoDont>

<DoDont>
  <Do>
    Maintain consistent button variants and sizes inside a single group container.
  </Do>
  <Dont>
    Never mix conflicting heights (`size="sm"` with `size="lg"`) within the same button group.
  </Dont>
</DoDont>

## API reference

<ApiTable components={['ButtonGroup']} />

## Related

- [Button](/ui/docs/components/actions/button) — Individual interactive action trigger.
- [ToggleGroup](/ui/docs/components/actions/toggle-group) — Connected group of toggle buttons for selection states.
- [Pagination](/ui/docs/components/navigation/pagination) — High-level navigation control for multi-page data sets.

## Button (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/actions/button)

Foundation action trigger supporting multiple semantic variants, sizes, loading spinners, and render polymorphism.

import { ButtonPlayground } from '@/components/docs/button-playground';
import { VariantCards, SizesDemo, IconsDemo, LoadingDemo, DisabledDemo, AsLinkDemo } from '@/components/docs/button-demos';

Buttons allow users to execute single-tap operations, submit forms, confirm transactions, and trigger dialogues. Built on Base UI's button primitive, `@innostes/ui` buttons guarantee visible keyboard focus rings, proper disabled state semantics, and render polymorphism without invalid DOM nesting.

<ComponentPreview name="actions/button/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import { Button, buttonVariants } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

- **Use Button** for operational actions such as saving records, approving purchase orders, opening modals, or deleting items.
- **Use Link or Button with `render`** when navigating to a new URL or page route.
- **Use ButtonGroup** when grouping closely related actions into a single segmented bar (e.g. Save, Save and submit).
- **Use Toggle or ToggleGroup** when switching a two-state option on or off, or selecting from a mutual exclusion set.

## Anatomy

<Anatomy
  slots={[
    { name: 'root', description: 'The outer button element (native button or custom render element)', dataSlot: 'button' },
    { name: 'spinner', description: 'Animated loading indicator rendered during active state', dataSlot: 'button-spinner' },
    { name: 'start-icon', description: 'Leading icon slot aligned with typography', dataSlot: 'button-icon-start' },
    { name: 'end-icon', description: 'Trailing icon slot aligned with typography', dataSlot: 'button-icon-end' },
  ]}
/>

## Examples

### Interactive playground

Experiment with button props, variants, and interactive states:

<ButtonPlayground />

### Variants

Use `variant` to express visual hierarchy:

<VariantCards />

```tsx
<Button variant="primary">Approve PO</Button>
<Button variant="secondary">Filter view</Button>
<Button variant="outline">Export CSV</Button>
<Button variant="ghost">Cancel</Button>
<Button variant="destructive">Void invoice</Button>
<Button variant="link">Terms of supply</Button>
```

### Sizes

Choose from three standardized heights: `sm` (32px), `md` (40px, default), and `lg` (48px):

<SizesDemo />

```tsx
<Button size="sm">Compact (32px)</Button>
<Button size="md">Default (40px)</Button>
<Button size="lg">Large (48px)</Button>
```

### With icons

Add leading or trailing icons using `startIcon` and `endIcon`. For icon-only triggers, use `iconOnly` alongside an explicit `aria-label`:

<IconsDemo />

### Loading state

Display a spinning indicator and prevent accidental duplicate submissions:

<LoadingDemo />

### Disabled state

Deactivate interactions during invalid preconditions:

<DisabledDemo />

### As link

Render the button visually while rendering an underlying framework router link:

<AsLinkDemo />

## Accessibility

### Keyboard navigation

<KeyboardTable
  rows={[
    { key: 'Enter', action: 'Triggers the button click action or submits the enclosing form.' },
    { key: 'Space', action: 'Triggers the button click action and emits active button states.' },
    { key: 'Tab', action: 'Moves keyboard focus onto or away from the button in sequential reading order.' },
  ]}
/>

### Screen readers and ARIA

- **Native `<button>` element**: Guarantees standard button accessibility semantics in the accessibility tree.
- **Icon-only requirement**: When `iconOnly` is enabled, an accessible name **must** be provided via `aria-label`.
- **Loading state**: When `loading={true}` is set, the button receives `aria-busy="true"` and `disabled={true}`, preventing duplicate network invocations.

## Guidelines

<DoDont>
  <Do>
    Use descriptive, action-oriented verbs such as "Approve purchase order", "Save changes", or "Void invoice".
  </Do>
  <Dont>
    Never use vague labels such as "Click here", "Submit", or "OK" on enterprise action buttons.
  </Dont>
</DoDont>

<DoDont>
  <Do>
    Always supply an `aria-label` when using the `iconOnly` prop so screen readers describe the operation.
  </Do>
  <Dont>
    Never leave icon-only buttons unlabelled, or use decorative icons that duplicate neighbouring text labels.
  </Dont>
</DoDont>

## Actions (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/actions/index)

Core interactive controls for submitting forms, triggering commands, and toggling states.

import { CategoryGrid } from '@/components/docs/category-grid';

# Actions

Actions are the primary interactive building blocks across Northwind Traders Pvt Ltd's enterprise operations. They communicate intent, submit forms, open dialogs, and toggle feature states with clear visual feedback and full keyboard accessibility.

## Components

<CategoryGrid category="components/actions" />

## Usage guidelines

- **Hierarchy**: Use primary buttons for the main action on a screen (at most one primary action per view). Secondary and outline buttons accommodate alternative paths.
- **Icon placement**: Use start icons for directional or verb cues (e.g. "Export", "Add item"). Use end icons for continuation cues (e.g. "Next", "View details").
- **State indicators**: Always provide loading states for asynchronous API operations to prevent duplicate form submissions and maintain user certainty.

---

## Toggle Group (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/actions/toggle-group)

Segmented control managing single or multiple active states with roving tabindex and arrow-key navigation.

ToggleGroup coordinates a set of two-state toggle buttons. Built on Base UI's toggle group primitive, it supports both single-selection (e.g. text alignment, view modes) and multi-selection (e.g. text formatting options) with built-in roving focus management and keyboard arrow navigation.

<ComponentPreview name="actions/toggle-group/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import { ToggleGroup, ToggleGroupItem } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

- **Use ToggleGroup** when users need to switch between related view layouts (e.g. List vs Grid) or apply multiple independent formatting options (e.g. Bold, Italic, Underline).
- **Use RadioGroup** when selecting one option from a list within a standard form where standard radio button styling is required.
- **Use Tabs** when selecting an option switches an entire underlying panel or page view.
- **Use ButtonGroup** when grouping operational action buttons that trigger commands rather than maintaining state.

## Examples

### Single selection

In default mode, ToggleGroup operates with single selection:

```tsx
const [view, setView] = useState(['table']);

<ToggleGroup value={view} onValueChange={setView} aria-label="Inventory layout">
  <ToggleGroupItem value="table">Table view</ToggleGroupItem>
  <ToggleGroupItem value="kanban">Kanban board</ToggleGroupItem>
</ToggleGroup>
```

### Multiple selection

Enable the `multiple` prop to permit selecting more than one option concurrently:

```tsx
const [formatting, setFormatting] = useState(['bold', 'italic']);

<ToggleGroup
  multiple
  value={formatting}
  onValueChange={setFormatting}
  aria-label="Rich text formatting"
>
  <ToggleGroupItem value="bold" aria-label="Bold"><Bold className="size-4" /></ToggleGroupItem>
  <ToggleGroupItem value="italic" aria-label="Italic"><Italic className="size-4" /></ToggleGroupItem>
  <ToggleGroupItem value="underline" aria-label="Underline"><Underline className="size-4" /></ToggleGroupItem>
</ToggleGroup>
```

### Attached outline styling

Use `variant="outline"` to merge borders and join the items into a solid segmented control:

```tsx
<ToggleGroup variant="outline" defaultValue={['all']} aria-label="Status filter">
  <ToggleGroupItem value="all">All orders</ToggleGroupItem>
  <ToggleGroupItem value="pending">Pending</ToggleGroupItem>
  <ToggleGroupItem value="dispatched">Dispatched</ToggleGroupItem>
</ToggleGroup>
```

## Accessibility

### Keyboard navigation

<KeyboardTable
  rows={[
    { key: 'ArrowRight / ArrowDown', action: 'Moves focus to the next item in the group, wrapping to the start.' },
    { key: 'ArrowLeft / ArrowUp', action: 'Moves focus to the previous item in the group, wrapping to the end.' },
    { key: 'Space / Enter', action: 'Toggles the pressed state of the currently focused item.' },
    { key: 'Home / End', action: 'Jumps focus directly to the first or last item in the group.' },
    { key: 'Tab', action: 'Leaves the toggle group and moves focus to the next control outside the group.' },
  ]}
/>

### Screen readers and ARIA

- **Roving tabindex**: Only the active or focused item has `tabIndex={0}`; remaining items receive `tabIndex={-1}`, ensuring the entire group acts as a single tab stop in the DOM.
- **`role="group"`**: Automatically applied to the container alongside the provided `aria-label`.
- **`aria-pressed`**: Emitted on each item to announce active state changes to screen readers.

## Guidelines

<DoDont>
  <Do>
    Always provide an `aria-label` on `ToggleGroup` describing the group purpose (e.g. `aria-label="View mode"`).
  </Do>
  <Dont>
    Never use `ToggleGroup` for navigating between separate URLs; use `Tabs` or standard navigation links instead.
  </Dont>
</DoDont>

<DoDont>
  <Do>
    Provide an `aria-label` on each `ToggleGroupItem` when items contain only icons without text labels.
  </Do>
  <Dont>
    Never mix mutually exclusive options with multi-select toggles inside the same group container.
  </Dont>
</DoDont>

## API reference

<ApiTable components={['ToggleGroup', 'ToggleGroupItem']} baseUi="toggle-group" />

- [Tabs](/ui/docs/components/navigation/tabs) — Tabbed interface for swapping content panels.

## Toggle (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/actions/toggle)

Accessible two-state pressed button primitive for formatting toolbars, favorites, and view modes.

Toggle is a two-state interactive control built on Base UI's toggle primitive. Unlike a standard button that triggers an action and immediately resets, Toggle maintains a pressed or unpressed state reflected via `aria-pressed`. It is ideal for rich text editor toolbars, bookmarking records, and filtering table views.

<ComponentPreview name="actions/toggle/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import { Toggle, toggleVariants } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

- **Use Toggle** for binary options where the button itself displays its active state (e.g. bold formatting, bookmarking an invoice).
- **Use Switch** for binary preferences inside configuration forms where a toggle switch with a distinct track and thumb is expected.
- **Use Checkbox** for multi-item selection in data tables or form agreements.
- **Use ToggleGroup** when grouping multiple toggle buttons into a toolbar or single-choice segmented control.

## Examples

### Basic usage

Toggle supports both uncontrolled (`defaultPressed`) and controlled (`pressed`, `onPressedChange`) modes:

```tsx
// Uncontrolled
<Toggle defaultPressed aria-label="Toggle bold text">
  <Bold className="size-4" />
</Toggle>

// Controlled
<Toggle
  pressed={isBookmarked}
  onPressedChange={setIsBookmarked}
  aria-label="Bookmark purchase order"
>
  <Bookmark className="size-4" />
</Toggle>
```

### With text label

Toggles can pair icons with visible textual descriptions:

```tsx
<Toggle variant="outline" aria-label="Mark invoice as urgent">
  <AlertCircle className="size-4 me-1.5 text-amber-500" />
  <span>Mark urgent</span>
</Toggle>
```

### Sizes

Toggles support the standard `sm` (32px), `md` (40px, default), and `lg` (48px) size scale:

```tsx
<Toggle size="sm" aria-label="Compact toggle"><Pin className="size-3.5" /></Toggle>
<Toggle size="md" aria-label="Default toggle"><Pin className="size-4" /></Toggle>
<Toggle size="lg" aria-label="Large toggle"><Pin className="size-5" /></Toggle>
```

## Accessibility

### Keyboard navigation

<KeyboardTable
  rows={[
    { key: 'Space', action: 'Toggles the pressed state between on and off.' },
    { key: 'Enter', action: 'Toggles the pressed state between on and off.' },
    { key: 'Tab', action: 'Moves focus to the toggle or away to the next interactive control.' },
  ]}
/>

### Screen readers and ARIA

- **`aria-pressed`**: Emits `aria-pressed="true"` when active and `aria-pressed="false"` when inactive. Screen readers announce "pressed" or "not pressed" immediately.
- **Icon-only requirement**: When a toggle contains only an icon glyph, an accessible name **must** be provided via `aria-label`.
- **Disabled state**: Applies `disabled` and `aria-disabled="true"` to prevent state changes.

## Guidelines

<DoDont>
  <Do>
    Provide an `aria-label` describing the state being toggled when no visible text is present (e.g. `aria-label="Toggle italic text"`).
  </Do>
  <Dont>
    Never use `Toggle` for irreversible operational actions such as deleting records or submitting forms; use `Button` instead.
  </Dont>
</DoDont>

<DoDont>
  <Do>
    Use `Toggle` when changes take effect immediately without requiring a separate "Save" form submission.
  </Do>
  <Dont>
    Never nest a `Toggle` inside a standard form where users expect explicit submit button confirmation.
  </Dont>
</DoDont>

## API reference

<ApiTable components={['Toggle']} baseUi="toggle" />

- [ToggleGroup](/ui/docs/components/actions/toggle-group) — Grouped collection of toggle buttons for toolbar selection.
- [Switch](/ui/docs/components/forms/switch) — Binary on/off control with physical switch semantics.
- [Button](/ui/docs/components/actions/button) — Foundation action trigger.

---

## Avatar (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/data-display/avatar)

Image avatar with graceful fallback initials, circular and square geometries, and overlapping avatar groups built on Base UI.

<ComponentPreview name="data-display/avatar/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import {
  Avatar,
  AvatarImage,
  AvatarFallback,
  AvatarGroup,
  type AvatarProps,
  type AvatarGroupProps,
} from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `Avatar` to visually represent individual team members, users, organizations, or products:

- Displaying user profiles in top navigation headers, comment threads, and activity logs.
- Indicating assignees on purchase orders, warehouse tasks, and approval chains.
- Representing vendors or partner organizations with square company logos.

When choosing avatar components:
- Use `Avatar` for user portraits and fallback initials.
- Use `shape="circle"` for individuals and `shape="square"` for enterprise entities, business units, or product lines.
- Use [IconTile](/ui/docs/components/data-display/icon-tile) when presenting a category or system module with a Lucide icon rather than a personal photo or initials.

## Examples

### Basic avatar with image and fallback

Compose `Avatar` with `AvatarImage` and `AvatarFallback`. If the image URL fails to load or is loading over a slow connection, `AvatarFallback` renders smoothly in its place.

```tsx
import { Avatar, AvatarImage, AvatarFallback } from '@innostes/ui';

export function UserAvatar() {
  return (
    <Avatar>
      <AvatarImage
        src="https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1534528741775-53994a69daeb?w=80&h=80&fit=crop&crop=face"
        alt="Priya Sharma"
      />
      <AvatarFallback>PS</AvatarFallback>
    </Avatar>
  );
}
```

### Avatar sizes and shapes

`Avatar` provides four standard sizes: `xs` (24px), `sm` (32px), `md` (40px, default), and `lg` (56px). Use `shape="square"` with rounded corners for companies and tenant workspaces:

```tsx
import { Avatar, AvatarFallback } from '@innostes/ui';

export function AvatarVariants() {
  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-4">
      <Avatar size="xs"><AvatarFallback>XS</AvatarFallback></Avatar>
      <Avatar size="sm"><AvatarFallback>SM</AvatarFallback></Avatar>
      <Avatar size="md"><AvatarFallback>MD</AvatarFallback></Avatar>
      <Avatar size="lg" shape="square"><AvatarFallback>NW</AvatarFallback></Avatar>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Avatar fallback delay

Provide a `delay` (in milliseconds) on `AvatarFallback` to prevent a brief visual flash of initials when images load quickly from browser cache.

```tsx
import { Avatar, AvatarImage, AvatarFallback } from '@innostes/ui';

export function DelayedFallbackAvatar() {
  return (
    <Avatar>
      <AvatarImage src="/photos/rajesh-nair.jpg" alt="Rajesh Nair" />
      <AvatarFallback delay={300}>RN</AvatarFallback>
    </Avatar>
  );
}
```

### Overlapping avatar groups

Wrap multiple avatars inside `AvatarGroup` to render an overlapping stack. Set `max` to limit the visible avatars, automatically rendering a trailing "+N" overflow counter pill.

```tsx
import { Avatar, AvatarFallback, AvatarGroup } from '@innostes/ui';

const assignees = ['Priya Sharma', 'Rajesh Nair', 'Ananya Rao', 'Vikram Patel'];

export function TaskAssignees() {
  return (
    <AvatarGroup max={3}>
      {assignees.map((name) => (
        <Avatar key={name} title={name}>
          <AvatarFallback>
            {name.split(' ').map((n) => n[0]).join('')}
          </AvatarFallback>
        </Avatar>
      ))}
    </AvatarGroup>
  );
}
```

## Accessibility

`Avatar` is built on Base UI Avatar primitives (`@base-ui/react/avatar`).

### Accessible naming and decorative images

- When an avatar appears next to a visible username or textual label (such as in a user menu or table row), set `alt=""` on `AvatarImage`. This marks the image as decorative, preventing screen readers from announcing redundant duplicate names.
- When an avatar appears as a standalone element without adjacent text, provide a descriptive `alt` attribute on `AvatarImage` (e.g. `alt="Priya Sharma"`) or pass an `aria-label` on `Avatar`.
- The overflow counter in `AvatarGroup` renders with an accessible label (`moreLabel`, defaulting to `(n) => "${n} more"`).

### Screen readers

- Fallback initials are rendered in uppercase and announced plainly.
- If an image fails to load, the DOM smoothly switches to the fallback element without breaking focus or emitting broken image placeholder graphics.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Use two uppercase initials for fallback avatars derived from the user’s first and last names (e.g., "PS").',
    code: `<AvatarFallback>{getInitials(user.fullName)}</AvatarFallback>`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not render long strings or full email addresses inside avatar fallback containers.',
    code: `<AvatarFallback>{user.email}</AvatarFallback> // Text overflows container`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Set shape="square" for company brands, vendor logos, or warehouse entities, reserving circles for people.',
    code: `<Avatar shape="square"><AvatarFallback>NW</AvatarFallback></Avatar>`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not use circular portraits for corporate entity logos with rectangular aspect ratios.',
    code: `<Avatar shape="circle"><AvatarImage src="/logos/vendor.png" /></Avatar>`,
  }}
/>

## API reference

<ApiTable
  components={['Avatar', 'AvatarImage', 'AvatarFallback', 'AvatarGroup']}
  baseUi="avatar"
/>

## Related

- [Card](/ui/docs/components/data-display/card) — Bordered container for user profiles and team member listings.
- [Badge](/ui/docs/components/data-display/badge) — Compact label for roles and status pills.
- [IconTile](/ui/docs/components/data-display/icon-tile) — Structured tile for displaying icons rather than user photos.

## Badge (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/data-display/badge)

Semantic status indicators with soft tinted backgrounds, contrast-hardened ring tokens, and optional pulse dots.

<ComponentPreview name="data-display/badge/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import { Badge, badgeVariants, type BadgeProps, type BadgeVariant } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `Badge` to communicate entity lifecycle states, categories, or numeric item counts:

- Displaying transaction states: Paid, Pending, Reconciled, Dispatched, or Overdue.
- Tagging categories or product groups (e.g. "Consumables", "Raw Materials").
- Showing auxiliary count indicators on tabs, table filters, or list items.

When choosing status components:
- Use `Badge` for passive inline status indicators and non-clickable labels.
- Use [TagInput](/ui/docs/components/forms/tag-input) when users need to create, type, and dismiss removable keyword tags.
- Use [StatusBadge](/ui/docs/components/actions/button) or [Alert](/ui/docs/components/feedback/alert) when displaying high-priority system announcements that require user remediation.

## Examples

### Semantic variants

`Badge` provides semantic variants aligned to administrative task statuses: `default`, `secondary`, `outline`, `success`, `warning`, `destructive`, and `info`. Soft variants use a tinted background combined with an inset ring token to maintain high visual contrast in dense tables without visual clutter.

```tsx
import { Badge } from '@innostes/ui';

export function StatusVariants() {
  return (
    <div className="flex gap-2">
      <Badge variant="success">Completed</Badge>
      <Badge variant="warning">Awaiting approval</Badge>
      <Badge variant="destructive">Payment failed</Badge>
      <Badge variant="info">In review</Badge>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Status indicator dot

Add `dot={true}` to render a small circular indicator preceding the label text. This reinforces live or operational state (e.g. online servers, open dispatches).

```tsx
import { Badge } from '@innostes/ui';

export function LiveStatusBadges() {
  return (
    <div className="flex gap-2">
      <Badge variant="success" dot>Live node</Badge>
      <Badge variant="warning" dot>Syncing</Badge>
      <Badge variant="destructive" dot>Offline</Badge>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Sizes and count badges

Choose between `size="md"` (default, 24px height) for general pages and `size="sm"` (20px height) for dense tables and compact count indicators:

```tsx
import { Badge } from '@innostes/ui';

export function CountBadges() {
  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
      <span className="text-sm font-medium">Pending requisitions</span>
      <Badge size="sm" variant="secondary">
        14
      </Badge>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Table cell status mapping

Define a type-safe mapping dictionary once in your domain types to translate backend entity statuses directly into badge variants:

```tsx
import { Badge, type BadgeVariant } from '@innostes/ui';

type OrderStatus = 'Draft' | 'Confirmed' | 'Dispatched' | 'Cancelled';

const statusMap: Record<OrderStatus, { variant: BadgeVariant; label: string }> = {
  Draft: { variant: 'secondary', label: 'Draft' },
  Confirmed: { variant: 'info', label: 'Confirmed' },
  Dispatched: { variant: 'success', label: 'Dispatched' },
  Cancelled: { variant: 'destructive', label: 'Cancelled' },
};

export function OrderStatusCell({ status }: { status: OrderStatus }) {
  const { variant, label } = statusMap[status];
  return <Badge variant={variant} dot>{label}</Badge>;
}
```

## Accessibility

`Badge` complies with WCAG 2.2 AA contrast standards across all semantic variants.

### Contrast and color independence

- Never rely exclusively on background color to communicate status. Always provide unambiguous text labels (e.g. "Overdue" rather than just a red dot or empty square).
- Every variant pairs text color and background tint with an inset ring token to guarantee 4.5:1 text-to-background contrast in both light and dark display modes.
- The indicator dot includes `aria-hidden="true"`, ensuring screen readers announce the semantic text directly without reading spurious bullet symbols.

### Screen readers

When badges are used as standalone status indicators without adjoining explanatory text, ensure parent containers or table cells provide adequate context via table headers or surrounding descriptions.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Use explicit, unambiguous text labels for every status badge (e.g. "Payment cleared", "Failed verification").',
    code: `<Badge variant="success">Cleared</Badge>`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not use badges with cryptic numeric codes or isolated colored dots without explanatory text.',
    code: `<Badge variant="destructive">ERR_504</Badge>`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Use the dot prop to signal real-time connectivity or operational lifecycle state.',
    code: `<Badge variant="success" dot>Active webhook</Badge>`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not use dot badges for static categories or unchanging product tags.',
    code: `<Badge dot>Beverages</Badge> // Static category does not need a live status dot`,
  }}
/>

## API reference

<ApiTable components={['Badge']} />

## Related

- [Data Table](/ui/docs/components/data-display/data-table) — Interactive data grid where badges represent row statuses.
- [TagInput](/ui/docs/components/forms/tag-input) — Removable keyword tags for categorization.
- [Alert](/ui/docs/components/feedback/alert) — Prominent contextual message banners.

## Card (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/data-display/card)

Structured card container composed of header, title, description, actions, content, and footer primitives.

<ComponentPreview name="data-display/card/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import {
  Card,
  CardHeader,
  CardTitle,
  CardDescription,
  CardAction,
  CardContent,
  CardFooter,
} from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `Card` to visually group related information, media, and actions into a distinct thematic container:

- Displaying overview KPI metrics, summary dashboards, and warehouse station cards.
- Segmenting settings panels, user profile details, and account configuration blocks.
- Grouping entity summaries, such as vendor profiles, customer order headers, and shipment tracking cards.

When choosing container components:
- Use `Card` when content needs a distinct bordered boundary with structured header, body, and footer areas.
- Use [Fieldset](/ui/docs/components/forms/field) when grouping form input controls under a semantic HTML `<legend>`.
- Use [WidgetCard](/ui/docs/widgets/widget-card) when building interactive dashboard widgets with built-in refresh actions, collapse controls, and loading overlays.

## Examples

### Basic card structure

Compose `Card` with `CardHeader`, `CardTitle`, `CardDescription`, and `CardContent`:

```tsx
import {
  Card,
  CardHeader,
  CardTitle,
  CardDescription,
  CardContent,
} from '@innostes/ui';

export function StorageLocationCard() {
  return (
    <Card>
      <CardHeader>
        <CardTitle>Bengaluru Central Warehouse</CardTitle>
        <CardDescription>Zone B · Cold Storage Facility</CardDescription>
      </CardHeader>
      <CardContent>
        <p className="text-sm">Current temperature: -18°C. Capacity utilization: 82%.</p>
      </CardContent>
    </Card>
  );
}
```

### Header actions

Place buttons, icon triggers, or dropdown menus inside `CardAction`. The card header uses an internal CSS grid layout that automatically positions actions in the top-end corner alongside title and description.

```tsx
import {
  Button,
  Card,
  CardHeader,
  CardTitle,
  CardDescription,
  CardAction,
  CardContent,
} from '@innostes/ui';

export function ActionableCard() {
  return (
    <Card>
      <CardHeader>
        <CardTitle>GST compliance certificate</CardTitle>
        <CardDescription>Valid through 31 March 2027</CardDescription>
        <CardAction>
          <Button size="sm" variant="outline">
            Renew
          </Button>
        </CardAction>
      </CardHeader>
      <CardContent>
        <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
          Filing status: Verified by GSTN authority.
        </p>
      </CardContent>
    </Card>
  );
}
```

### Content with footer metadata

Use `CardFooter` to display auxiliary metadata, timestamps, or secondary action buttons along the bottom margin.

```tsx
import {
  Card,
  CardHeader,
  CardTitle,
  CardContent,
  CardFooter,
  Button,
} from '@innostes/ui';

export function ShipmentSummary() {
  return (
    <Card>
      <CardHeader>
        <CardTitle>Consignment #KA-8902</CardTitle>
      </CardHeader>
      <CardContent>
        <p className="text-sm">Carrier: Blue Dart Express. Destination: Whitefield Depot.</p>
      </CardContent>
      <CardFooter className="flex justify-between items-center text-xs text-muted-foreground">
        <span>Updated 12 minutes ago</span>
        <Button size="sm" variant="ghost">Track manifest</Button>
      </CardFooter>
    </Card>
  );
}
```

### Document heading hierarchy

`CardTitle` renders a `<div>` element by default to avoid dictating document heading levels. When the title represents a structural section of the document, nest an appropriate heading tag (`<h2>`, `<h3>`) inside `CardTitle`:

```tsx
import { Card, CardHeader, CardTitle, CardContent } from '@innostes/ui';

export function AccessibleHeadingCard() {
  return (
    <Card>
      <CardHeader>
        <CardTitle>
          <h2 className="text-base font-semibold">Security credentials</h2>
        </CardTitle>
      </CardHeader>
      <CardContent>
        <p className="text-sm">Two-factor authentication is enabled for all administrators.</p>
      </CardContent>
    </Card>
  );
}
```

## Accessibility

`Card` components provide flexible container semantics without enforcing rigid landmark structures.

### Semantic heading structure

- Because cards can be used anywhere from top-level page views to deeply nested sidebars, `CardTitle` renders an unstyled container by default. Nest an `<h2>`, `<h3>`, or `<h4>` element inside `CardTitle` to ensure screen reader users can navigate through cards via standard heading rotor shortcuts.
- Avoid nesting interactive cards inside another clickable card to prevent nested interactive controls (`button` inside `button`).

### Screen readers

- When actions are embedded in `CardAction`, ensure buttons include explicit accessible names (e.g. `aria-label="Edit warehouse settings"` instead of a bare icon).
- Cards with critical status indicators should pair visual badges with descriptive textual context.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Place primary section triggers or menus inside CardAction to guarantee consistent top-end alignment.',
    code: `<CardHeader>\n  <CardTitle>Billing</CardTitle>\n  <CardAction><Button size="sm">Manage</Button></CardAction>\n</CardHeader>`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not position action buttons manually with absolute coordinates inside the card container.',
    code: `<div className="relative">\n  <button className="absolute top-2 right-2">Edit</button>\n</div>`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Nest semantic HTML heading tags (such as <h3>) inside CardTitle when the card represents a section in document flow.',
    code: `<CardTitle><h3>Tax settings</h3></CardTitle>`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not skip heading hierarchy levels on the host page when authoring card titles.',
    code: `// Avoid placing <h5> immediately following an <h1>`,
  }}
/>

<ApiTable
  components={[
    'Card',
    'CardHeader',
    'CardTitle',
    'CardDescription',
    'CardAction',
    'CardContent',
    'CardFooter',
  ]}
/>

- [Table](/ui/docs/components/data-display/table) — Semantic HTML table for tabular summaries.
- [WidgetCard](/ui/docs/widgets/widget-card) — Dashboard widget card with collapse and loading states.

## Data Table (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/data-display/data-table)

Rich data grid supporting typed columns, multi-row selection, server-side data fetching, skeleton loading, and container-query mobile card transformations.

<ComponentPreview name="data-display/data-table/basic" align="start" />

## Import

```tsx
import {
  DataTable,
  type DataTableColumn,
  type DataTableProps,
  type DataTableSlot,
  type SortState,
  type SortValue,
} from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `DataTable` when operators need to browse, filter, sort, select, and manage structured tabular datasets in administrative interfaces:

- Managing core business entities: sales orders, inventory balances, purchase requisitions, and vendor master data.
- Handling paginated server records with sorting, pagination, and bulk batch actions.
- Displaying tabular data that transforms into responsive stacked cards on mobile devices.

When deciding between table implementations:
- Use [Table](/ui/docs/components/data-display/table) when rendering static, short tabular data (such as invoice line item breakdowns or tax summary blocks) where column sorting, multi-selection, and pagination controls are unnecessary.
- Use `DataTable` for entity listings, audit logs, and search results requiring pagination, multi-row selection, or dynamic sorting.
- For extremely large datasets with more than 1,000 simultaneous unpaginated rows rendered in the DOM, combine `Table` with virtual scrolling (`@tanstack/react-virtual`).

## Examples

### Typed columns and accessor mapping

Columns are generic over your row type `TRow`. Define `id`, `header`, `accessor` (used for sorting and default text extraction), and optional custom `cell` render functions.

```tsx
import { Badge, DataTable, type DataTableColumn } from '@innostes/ui';

interface PurchaseOrder {
  id: string;
  vendor: string;
  status: 'Draft' | 'Approved' | 'Dispatched';
  totalAmount: number;
}

const columns: DataTableColumn<PurchaseOrder>[] = [
  {
    id: 'id',
    header: 'PO number',
    accessor: (row) => row.id,
    sortable: true,
    cell: (row) => <span className="font-mono font-medium">{row.id}</span>,
  },
  {
    id: 'vendor',
    header: 'Vendor name',
    accessor: (row) => row.vendor,
    sortable: true,
  },
  {
    id: 'status',
    header: 'Status',
    accessor: (row) => row.status,
    cell: (row) => (
      <Badge variant={row.status === 'Approved' ? 'success' : 'secondary'}>
        {row.status}
      </Badge>
    ),
  },
  {
    id: 'totalAmount',
    header: 'Amount',
    accessor: (row) => row.totalAmount,
    sortable: true,
    align: 'end',
    cell: (row) => (
      <span className="font-mono">
        ₹{row.totalAmount.toLocaleString('en-IN')}
      </span>
    ),
  },
];
```

### Number and currency alignment

Numerical quantities, percentages, and monetary values must always align to the right (`align="end"`). This ensures decimal points and magnitude digits align vertically for rapid visual scanning by accounting operators.

```tsx
const columns: DataTableColumn<InvoiceItem>[] = [
  {
    id: 'quantity',
    header: 'Quantity',
    accessor: (r) => r.quantity,
    align: 'end',
    cell: (r) => <span className="tabular-nums">{r.quantity}</span>,
  },
  {
    id: 'unitPrice',
    header: 'Unit price',
    accessor: (r) => r.unitPrice,
    align: 'end',
    cell: (r) => (
      <span className="tabular-nums">₹{r.unitPrice.toFixed(2)}</span>
    ),
  },
];
```

### Server-side pagination and sorting

When operating on database datasets with thousands of records, set `manualSorting={true}` and `manualPagination={true}`. Pass the current slice of data as `data`, the overall record count as `totalCount`, and handle state transitions through `onSortChange` and `onPageChange`.

<ComponentPreview name="data-display/data-table/server-side" align="start" />

```tsx
'use client';

import { useState, useEffect } from 'react';
import { DataTable, type SortState } from '@innostes/ui';

export function ServerOrdersTable() {
  const [data, setData] = useState([]);
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true);
  const [page, setPage] = useState(1);
  const [sort, setSort] = useState<SortState | null>({
    columnId: 'date',
    direction: 'desc',
  });
  const [totalCount, setTotalCount] = useState(0);

  useEffect(() => {
    let cancelled = false;
    setLoading(true);

    fetch(`/api/v1/orders?page=${page}&sort=${sort?.columnId}&dir=${sort?.direction}`)
      .then((res) => res.json())
      .then((json) => {
        if (!cancelled) {
          setData(json.items);
          setTotalCount(json.total);
          setLoading(false);
        }
      });

    return () => {
      cancelled = true;
    };
  }, [page, sort]);

  return (
    <DataTable
      aria-label="Server purchase orders"
      data={data}
      columns={columns}
      getRowId={(row) => row.id}
      loading={loading}
      page={page}
      onPageChange={setPage}
      pageSize={10}
      manualPagination
      totalCount={totalCount}
      sort={sort}
      onSortChange={setSort}
      manualSorting
    />
  );
}
```

### Selection and bulk actions

Enable multi-row checkbox selection by setting `selectable={true}`. Pass `selectedIds` and `onSelectedIdsChange` to control the active set of selected IDs.

```tsx
'use client';

import { useState } from 'react';
import { Button, DataTable, toast } from '@innostes/ui';

export function BulkDispatchTable({ orders, columns }) {
  const [selectedIds, setSelectedIds] = useState<string[]>([]);

  const handleBulkDispatch = () => {
    toast.success(`Dispatched ${selectedIds.length} orders successfully.`);
    setSelectedIds([]);
  };

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-4">
      <div className="flex justify-between items-center">
        <span className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
          {selectedIds.length} orders selected
        </span>
        <Button
          size="sm"
          disabled={selectedIds.length === 0}
          onClick={handleBulkDispatch}
        >
          Dispatch selected
        </Button>
      </div>

      <DataTable
        aria-label="Orders awaiting dispatch"
        data={orders}
        columns={columns}
        getRowId={(row) => row.id}
        selectable
        selectedIds={selectedIds}
        onSelectedIdsChange={setSelectedIds}
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Loading and empty states

Supply custom `emptyState` messages or let `DataTable` display animated skeleton rows when `loading={true}`.

<ComponentPreview name="data-display/data-table/loading" align="start" />

```tsx
<DataTable
  aria-label="Pending payments"
  data={[]}
  columns={columns}
  getRowId={(r) => r.id}
  loading={isLoading}
  loadingRowCount={6}
  emptyState="No pending payments found for this ledger period."
/>
```

### Responsive stack mode

On narrow mobile displays or tight dashboard containers, set `responsive="stack"`. The table uses container queries (`@container`) to automatically transform horizontal table rows into card-based key-value pairs without requiring viewport breakpoint hacks.

```tsx
<DataTable
  aria-label="Mobile inventory list"
  data={stockItems}
  columns={columns}
  getRowId={(r) => r.id}
  responsive="stack"
/>
```

## Accessibility

`DataTable` adheres to W3C WAI-ARIA Table and Grid accessibility standards.

### Keyboard navigation

<KeyboardTable
  entries={[
    { key: 'Tab', action: 'Moves focus sequentially between sortable column header buttons, row selection checkboxes, row action triggers, and pagination buttons.' },
    { key: 'Enter / Space', action: 'Toggles sorting on a focused header button or toggles row selection on a checkbox.' },
  ]}
/>

### Screen readers and announcements

- Real semantic HTML `<table>`, `<thead>`, `<tbody>`, `<th>`, and `<td>` elements ensure assistive technologies correctly identify row and column counts.
- Column headers with sorting enabled render an embedded `<button>` element with `aria-sort="ascending"`, `aria-sort="descending"`, or `aria-sort="none"`.
- Row selection checkboxes carry localized accessible labels (e.g. "Select row PO-8410").
- The master checkbox uses `aria-label="Select all rows on this page"` and reflects indeterminate state when a subset of page rows is selected.
- A live region announces changes in selection counts politely.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Always align numerical values, currency figures, and quantities to the right (align="end") and wrap them with tabular-nums.',
    code: `{ id: 'amount', header: 'Total', align: 'end', accessor: (r) => r.amount }`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not left-align currency figures or numerical measurements in data tables, as jagged digits impede visual comparison.',
    code: `{ id: 'amount', header: 'Total', align: 'start' }`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Provide an aria-label attribute describing the table contents (e.g., aria-label="Customer invoices").',
    code: `<DataTable aria-label="Vendor purchase orders" data={orders} ... />`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not omit accessible naming on tables; screen readers will identify them merely as generic unnamed tables.',
    code: `<DataTable data={orders} ... />`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Use manualPagination and manualSorting when querying database tables with more than 100 rows.',
    code: `<DataTable manualPagination manualSorting totalCount={totalCount} ... />`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not download 10,000 records to the client browser to perform client-side sorting and pagination.',
    code: `// Anti-pattern: High network transfer and memory overhead\nconst allRecords = await fetchAllRecords();`,
  }}
/>

## API reference

<ApiTable components={['DataTable']} />

## Related

- [Table](/ui/docs/components/data-display/table) — Semantic HTML table primitives for simple tabular content.
- [Pagination](/ui/docs/components/navigation/pagination) — Standalone pagination controls.
- [Badge](/ui/docs/components/data-display/badge) — Status and category indicators for table cells.
- [Empty State](/ui/docs/components/data-display/empty-state) — Empty placeholder representations.

## Empty State (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/data-display/empty-state)

Clean empty state representation with icon container, title, explanatory description, and primary/secondary action triggers.

<ComponentPreview name="data-display/empty-state/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import { EmptyState, type EmptyStateProps, type EmptyStateSlot } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `EmptyState` when a view, list, table, or search panel contains no records to present:

- **First-use onboarding**: Introducing a blank module (e.g. "No purchase orders yet") and guiding the user to create their first record.
- **Zero search or filter matches**: Explaining that a query returned no results and providing a one-click action to reset active filters.
- **Completed queues**: Congratulating an operator when an inbox or approval queue has been fully cleared.
- **Permission boundaries**: Explaining that the current user account does not have authorization to view records in this section.

When choosing empty representation:
- Use `EmptyState` inside tables, cards, and page views when space permits an icon, title, and action buttons.
- Use a concise string or empty message inside small dropdown menus (such as [Select](/ui/docs/components/forms/select) or [Combobox](/ui/docs/components/forms/combobox)).
- Refer to the [Feedback decision guide](/ui/docs/components/feedback) for cross-component guidance on when to choose between alerts, empty states, and dialogs.

## Examples

### First use / blank canvas

Provide a welcoming title, a brief explanation of how records are populated, and primary action buttons to create or import records:

```tsx
import { Button, EmptyState } from '@innostes/ui';
import { FilePlus, Upload } from 'lucide-react';

export function InitialInvoicesEmptyState() {
  return (
    <EmptyState
      icon={<FilePlus />}
      title="No purchase orders created"
      description="Create your first purchase order or import batch requisitions from your ERP spreadsheet."
      actions={
        <>
          <Button variant="outline" startIcon={<Upload />}>
            Import CSV
          </Button>
          <Button startIcon={<FilePlus />}>
            Create purchase order
          </Button>
        </>
      }
    />
  );
}
```

### No search or filter results

When active filters produce zero records, reassure the operator that data exists and offer a clear filter reset trigger:

```tsx
'use client';

import { Button, EmptyState } from '@innostes/ui';
import { SearchX } from 'lucide-react';

export function FilterEmptyState({ onReset }: { onReset: () => void }) {
  return (
    <EmptyState
      icon={<SearchX />}
      title="No matching invoices found"
      description="No records match your active date range and vendor filters. Try clearing filters to see all invoices."
      actions={
        <Button variant="outline" onClick={onReset}>
          Reset active filters
        </Button>
      }
    />
  );
}
```

### Permission or access restriction

When an operator lacks role-based permissions, clarify the restriction and indicate which department or administrator can grant access:

```tsx
import { Button, EmptyState } from '@innostes/ui';
import { ShieldAlert } from 'lucide-react';

export function RestrictedEmptyState() {
  return (
    <EmptyState
      icon={<ShieldAlert />}
      title="Restricted ledger view"
      description="Your user profile does not have clearance to view executive payroll ledgers. Contact your compliance administrator to request access."
      actions={
        <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => window.location.href = 'mailto:compliance@northwindtraders.in'}>
          Request clearance
        </Button>
      }
    />
  );
}
```

### Data table integration

Pass `EmptyState` directly to `DataTable` via its `emptyState` prop:

```tsx
<DataTable
  aria-label="Purchase requisitions"
  data={[]}
  columns={columns}
  getRowId={(r) => r.id}
  emptyState={
    <EmptyState
      title="No open requisitions"
      description="All procurement requisitions for this quarter have been processed."
    />
  }
/>
```

## Accessibility

`EmptyState` uses accessible heading structure and semantic action layout.

### Heading hierarchy

- `title` renders inside an `<h3>` heading element by default.
- When placed within a top-level page landmark that lacks intermediate headings, you can customize the title element using `classNames.title` or nest an appropriate heading level (`<h2>`) within `title`.

### Focus management and action clarity

- Action buttons inside `actions` receive standard keyboard tab navigation.
- Ensure action button labels clearly communicate destination or consequence (e.g. "Create purchase order" instead of generic "Create").
- Icons are wrapped in an `aria-hidden` container to avoid announcing decorative icon names to screen reader users.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Always provide an actionable next step, such as a "Create record" or "Reset filters" button.',
    code: `<EmptyState title="No vendors found" actions={<Button>Add vendor</Button>} />`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not leave the user at a dead end with passive text like "No data" and no recovery action.',
    code: `<EmptyState title="No data" /> // No guidance or recovery action`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Distinguish clearly between initial first-use (no records created yet) and zero search results (data exists, but query matched nothing).',
    code: `const title = hasFilter ? "No matching orders" : "No orders yet";`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not display "Create your first order" when a user simply mistyped an order number in a search bar.',
    code: `// Confusing: Tells user to create an order when search returns 0 results`,
  }}
/>

## API reference

<ApiTable components={['EmptyState']} />

## Related

- [Data Table](/ui/docs/components/data-display/data-table) — Interactive data grid supporting custom empty states.
- [Button](/ui/docs/components/actions/button) — Action buttons embedded in empty states.
- [Alert](/ui/docs/components/feedback/alert) — Persistent banners for operational warnings and messages.

## Icon Tile (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/data-display/icon-tile)

Visual icon container offering semantic and categorical chart tones, soft/solid treatments, and four standard sizes.

<ComponentPreview name="data-display/icon-tile/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import { IconTile, type IconTileProps, type IconTileTone } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `IconTile` to highlight an icon with a tinted or solid background container in dashboard summaries, module navigation lists, or feature cards:

- Categorizing ERP modules (Procurement, Inventory, Ledgers, Logistics) with dedicated palette colors.
- Visually anchoring metric tiles ([MetricCard](/ui/docs/widgets/metric-card) and [Stat](/ui/docs/components/data-display/stat)).
- Reinforcing empty state or workflow step headers with prominent iconography.

When choosing icon components:
- Use `IconTile` when an icon needs a dedicated square or circular background surface to aid visual scanning.
- Use raw SVG icons (from `lucide-react`) directly when rendering inline icon buttons or standard form input adornments.
- Use [Avatar](/ui/docs/components/data-display/avatar) when representing people, team members, or company logos.

## Examples

### Semantic and categorical tones

`IconTile` provides both semantic roles (`primary`, `success`, `warning`, `destructive`, `info`, `neutral`) and eight categorical chart tones (`chart-1` through `chart-8`). Categorical tones match design system charts, allowing dashboards to share uniform color coding across charts and tiles.

```tsx
import { IconTile } from '@innostes/ui';
import { Truck, ShieldCheck, AlertTriangle } from 'lucide-react';

export function SemanticTiles() {
  return (
    <div className="flex gap-3">
      <IconTile tone="primary"><Truck /></IconTile>
      <IconTile tone="success"><ShieldCheck /></IconTile>
      <IconTile tone="warning"><AlertTriangle /></IconTile>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Soft and solid variants

Choose between `variant="soft"` (default, tinted background with colored foreground icon) for subtle dashboard lists, and `variant="solid"` (bold, opaque fill) for primary callouts:

```tsx
import { IconTile } from '@innostes/ui';
import { Package, Warehouse } from 'lucide-react';

export function TileVariants() {
  return (
    <div className="flex gap-4">
      <IconTile tone="chart-1" variant="soft"><Package /></IconTile>
      <IconTile tone="chart-1" variant="solid"><Warehouse /></IconTile>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Sizes and shapes

`IconTile` supports four sizes: `sm` (32px), `md` (40px, default), `lg` (48px), and `xl` (56px). Set `shape="circle"` to render circular badges:

```tsx
import { IconTile } from '@innostes/ui';
import { Check, Shield } from 'lucide-react';

export function ShapeSizes() {
  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
      <IconTile size="sm" shape="circle" tone="success" variant="solid">
        <Check />
      </IconTile>
      <IconTile size="lg" shape="square" tone="info">
        <Shield />
      </IconTile>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Bordered tiles on tinted surfaces

When placing an icon tile on a tinted or card surface, add `bordered={true}` to introduce an inset ring token that maintains crisp silhouette definition:

```tsx
import { IconTile } from '@innostes/ui';
import { Bell } from 'lucide-react';

export function BorderedTile() {
  return (
    <div className="rounded-lg bg-muted/40 p-4">
      <IconTile tone="destructive" bordered>
        <Bell />
      </IconTile>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Accessibility

`IconTile` is strictly a presentation component.

### Decorative icons and aria-hidden

- Embedded icons render with `aria-hidden="true"` by default.
- `IconTile` itself is decorative. Never use an isolated `IconTile` without adjacent descriptive text (such as a card title or list label) or an explicit `aria-label` when wrapped inside an interactive container.

### Color contrast

All `soft` and `solid` variants meet WCAG 2.2 AA non-text contrast requirements (> 3:1 for graphical objects and boundaries) across light and dark display modes.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Maintain uniform categorical chart tones (chart-1 through chart-8) for specific ERP modules across navigation and charts.',
    code: `<IconTile tone="chart-2"><Package /></IconTile> // Consistent procurement blue`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not randomize categorical tones across different pages for the same business entity.',
    code: `// Confusing: changing module colors arbitrarily across screens\n<IconTile tone="chart-5"><Package /></IconTile>`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Always accompany IconTile with descriptive text, such as a metric label or navigation title.',
    code: `<div className="flex items-center gap-3">\n  <IconTile tone="primary"><Truck /></IconTile>\n  <span>Fleet dispatches</span>\n</div>`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not render bare icon tiles without adjoining labels or accessible text.',
    code: `<IconTile tone="primary"><Truck /></IconTile> // What does this tile represent?`,
  }}
/>

## API reference

<ApiTable components={['IconTile']} />

## Related

- [Stat](/ui/docs/components/data-display/stat) — Metric tiles that embed icon adornments.
- [MetricCard](/ui/docs/widgets/metric-card) — Interactive dashboard cards featuring icon tiles and sparklines.
- [Badge](/ui/docs/components/data-display/badge) — Textual status tags and pills.

## Data display (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/data-display/index)

Components for structured record presentation, hierarchies, and metric highlights.

import { CategoryGrid } from '@/components/docs/category-grid';

# Data display

Data display components structure and present information with high information density, clear typographic hierarchy, and accessible markup. From high-throughput financial tables to hierarchical organizational trees, these components present Northwind Traders Pvt Ltd's operational data with clarity.

## Components

<CategoryGrid category="components/data-display" />

## Best practices

- **Data tables**: Prefer `DataTable` for complex administrative tables requiring client-side pagination, sorting, row selection, and column toggling.
- **Empty states**: Always render an explicit `EmptyState` when collections, search queries, or filter combinations produce zero results.
- **Status indicators**: Use semantic badges (`success`, `warning`, `destructive`) consistently across data rows to reflect item lifecycles.

## Kbd (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/data-display/kbd)

Monospace key badge styled with borders and subtle elevation for communicating shortcuts in tooltips, menus, and help docs.

<ComponentPreview name="data-display/kbd/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import { Kbd } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `Kbd` to visually indicate keyboard shortcuts, keypress combinations, or hotkeys across the user interface:

- Displaying global shortcuts inside search triggers (e.g. `⌘` `K` or `Ctrl` `K`).
- Indicating keyboard actions in [DropdownMenu](/ui/docs/components/overlays/dropdown-menu) items.
- Formatting keyboard shortcut reference tables in administrative documentation.

When choosing text formatting:
- Use `Kbd` for physical hardware keys (`Enter`, `Esc`, `Tab`).
- Use inline `<code>` tags for code tokens, JSON keys, variable names, or CLI commands.

## Examples

### Single key and combinations

Render individual keys in separate `<Kbd>` components to indicate sequential or simultaneous keystrokes:

```tsx
import { Kbd } from '@innostes/ui';

export function NavigationShortcuts() {
  return (
    <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
      Press <Kbd>Shift</Kbd> + <Kbd>?</Kbd> to open shortcut help, or <Kbd>Esc</Kbd> to dismiss.
    </p>
  );
}
```

### Modifiers and cross-platform representations

Present modifier keys clearly. You can render macOS glyphs (`⌘`, `⌥`, `⇧`) or standard PC keys (`Ctrl`, `Alt`, `Shift`):

```tsx
import { Kbd } from '@innostes/ui';

export function CrossPlatformShortcuts() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-2 text-sm">
      <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
        <span className="w-24 text-muted-foreground">macOS:</span>
        <Kbd>⌘</Kbd> <Kbd>K</Kbd>
      </div>
      <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
        <span className="w-24 text-muted-foreground">Windows/Linux:</span>
        <Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd> + <Kbd>K</Kbd>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Shortcuts inside menus and tooltips

Combine `Kbd` within dropdown menus or tooltips to inform operators of available accelerators:

```tsx
import {
  DropdownMenu,
  DropdownMenuContent,
  DropdownMenuItem,
  DropdownMenuTrigger,
  Button,
  Kbd,
} from '@innostes/ui';

export function ShortcutMenu() {
  return (
    <DropdownMenu>
      <DropdownMenuTrigger render={<Button size="sm">File</Button>} />
      <DropdownMenuContent className="w-48">
        <DropdownMenuItem className="flex justify-between items-center">
          <span>Quick search</span>
          <div className="flex gap-1">
            <Kbd>⌘</Kbd><Kbd>K</Kbd>
          </div>
        </DropdownMenuItem>
      </DropdownMenuContent>
    </DropdownMenu>
  );
}
```

## Accessibility

`Kbd` renders a native HTML `<kbd>` element.

### Semantic kbd element

- The native `<kbd>` tag conveys keyboard input semantics to assistive technologies and web crawlers.
- `Kbd` components feature `select-none` and `pointer-events-none` styling so dragging across lines does not unintentionally highlight individual key caps.

### Screen readers and modifier announcements

- Screen readers announce the textual contents of `<kbd>` tags directly (e.g., "Control plus K").
- When using special symbol characters like `⌘` or `⌥`, ensure the parent container or surrounding prose includes an accessible label or textual clarification for screen readers that do not announce mathematical or typographical glyphs.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Render separate keys inside their own Kbd components (e.g. <Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd> + <Kbd>P</Kbd>).',
    code: `<Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd> + <Kbd>P</Kbd>`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not bundle key combinations into a single Kbd element.',
    code: `<Kbd>Ctrl + P</Kbd> // Renders as one monolithic key cap`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Use standard keyboard abbreviations (Ctrl, Alt, Shift, Esc, Tab, Enter).',
    code: `<Kbd>Esc</Kbd>`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not use colloquial names like "Escape Key" inside a small key cap.',
    code: `<Kbd>Escape Key</Kbd>`,
  }}
/>

## API reference

<ApiTable components={['Kbd']} />

## Related

- [CommandPalette](/ui/docs/components/overlays/command-palette) — Shortcut-driven global action launcher.
- [DropdownMenu](/ui/docs/components/overlays/dropdown-menu) — Menu lists that display hotkey accelerators.
- [Tooltip](/ui/docs/components/overlays/tooltip) — Hover tips containing keyboard shortcut reminders.
