## Stat (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/data-display/stat)

Compact KPI summary tile with automatic trend direction inference, customizable sentiment polarities, and icon slots.

<ComponentPreview name="data-display/stat/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import { Stat, type StatProps } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `Stat` to display high-level numeric metrics, KPIs, and summary totals on executive summaries or operational dashboards:

- Displaying monthly revenue, active purchase orders, warehouse dispatch volume, and inventory turnover.
- Presenting delta comparisons against a previous accounting period or baseline forecast.
- Highlighting operational metrics where an upward increase can represent either a positive gain or an unfavorable cost spike.

When choosing metric display components:
- Use `Stat` for single-value numeric summaries with delta arrows and contextual helper notes.
- Use [MetricCard](/ui/docs/widgets/metric-card) when you need to embed an inline sparkline or area chart directly inside the KPI tile.
- Use [Badge](/ui/docs/components/data-display/badge) when displaying a concise status or count directly inside a table cell or page header.

## Examples

### Basic metric tile

Provide a `label`, formatted numeric `value`, optional `delta` string (such as `"+12.5%"`), and `helper` text explaining the comparison baseline:

```tsx
import { Stat } from '@innostes/ui';

export function RevenueStat() {
  return (
    <Stat
      label="Gross revenue"
      value="₹84,50,000"
      delta="+18.4%"
      helper="vs previous fiscal quarter"
    />
  );
}
```

### Inverted trends with upIsGood

By default, an upward delta (`+`) is treated as positive (styled in `text-success` with a green arrow). For metrics where an increase is undesirable—such as warehouse return rates, defect counts, or average delivery delays—set `upIsGood={false}`. This renders an upward delta with a red arrow in `text-destructive`.

```tsx
import { Stat } from '@innostes/ui';

export function ReturnRateStat() {
  return (
    <Stat
      label="Consignment return rate"
      value="2.8%"
      delta="+0.6%"
      upIsGood={false}
      helper="exceeds target ceiling of 2.0%"
    />
  );
}
```

### Neutral trends and target comparisons

For metrics with negligible percentage deviation or when no direction arrow is desired, explicitly set `trend="neutral"`:

```tsx
import { Stat } from '@innostes/ui';

export function InventoryFillRate() {
  return (
    <Stat
      label="Warehouse fill rate"
      value="99.4%"
      delta="0.0%"
      trend="neutral"
      helper="unchanged from last week"
    />
  );
}
```

### Dashboard metric grid

Organize multiple `Stat` tiles in a responsive CSS grid layout:

```tsx
import { Stat } from '@innostes/ui';
import { Package, Truck, Clock } from 'lucide-react';

export function OperationsOverview() {
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-4 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3">
      <Stat
        label="Pending orders"
        value="142"
        delta="-8"
        helper="vs yesterday"
        icon={<Package />}
      />
      <Stat
        label="In-transit dispatches"
        value="58"
        delta="+12"
        helper="on schedule"
        icon={<Truck />}
      />
      <Stat
        label="Average turnaround"
        value="4.2 hrs"
        delta="-0.6 hrs"
        upIsGood={true}
        helper="dock-to-truck time"
        icon={<Clock />}
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Accessibility

`Stat` uses semantic markup and tabular numbers for readable metric presentations.

### Screen readers and trend indicators

- Trend arrows (`ArrowUpIcon`, `ArrowDownIcon`) are rendered with `aria-hidden="true"`.
- When delta text includes a leading `+` or `-` symbol, screen readers announce the numeric polarity cleanly without relying exclusively on color.
- Avoid using color alone to communicate whether a trend is favorable or unfavorable; ensure the helper text or label provides adequate context.

### Numerical tabular formatting

The big metric value renders with `tabular-nums` by default, ensuring monospace numeral widths that prevent layout jitter during dynamic ticker updates or real-time polling.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Set `upIsGood={false}` for negative business metrics like server errors, return rates, or customer churn.',
    code: `<Stat label="Rejection rate" delta="+1.2%" upIsGood={false} />`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not allow an increase in customer complaints or shipping damages to display with a green success arrow.',
    code: `<Stat label="Damaged cartons" delta="+14" /> // Defaults to green upward arrow`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Provide explicit helper text describing the reference baseline period (e.g. "vs previous month").',
    code: `<Stat label="Dispatched orders" value="1,240" delta="+8%" helper="vs previous month" />`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not present isolated delta percentages without clarifying what time window is being compared.',
    code: `<Stat label="Dispatched orders" value="1,240" delta="+8%" /> // Lacks baseline context`,
  }}
/>

## API reference

<ApiTable components={['Stat']} />

## Related

- [Card](/ui/docs/components/data-display/card) — Bordered content container.
- [Badge](/ui/docs/components/data-display/badge) — Status and numeric tags.
- [MetricCard](/ui/docs/widgets/metric-card) — Dashboard metric tile with embedded chart sparklines.

## Table (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/data-display/table)

Accessible HTML table building blocks for displaying custom tabular breakdowns, invoice summaries, and financial ledger items.

<ComponentPreview name="data-display/table/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import {
  Table,
  TableHeader,
  TableBody,
  TableFooter,
  TableRow,
  TableHead,
  TableCell,
  TableCaption,
  type TableProps,
} from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `Table` when you need direct, unopinionated JSX control over tabular markup for small, static datasets:

- Rendering invoice line item breakdowns, tax computation schedules, or cost allocations.
- Presenting simple reference charts or tabular key-value matrices (such as shipping fee tiers).
- Displaying short summaries (fewer than 20 rows) where dynamic column sorting, client pagination, and batch checkbox selection are not required.

When choosing between table components:
- Use `Table` when you want zero runtime overhead (< 1.5 KB), direct JSX composition, and complete freedom over row and column spans.
- Use [Data Table](/ui/docs/components/data-display/data-table) when you need column sorting, pagination, multi-row selection, search filtering, empty states, or mobile card transformations.

## Examples

### Basic table structure

Compose `Table` using standard HTML hierarchy: `TableHeader`, `TableBody`, `TableFooter`, `TableRow`, `TableHead`, and `TableCell`.

```tsx
import {
  Table,
  TableHeader,
  TableBody,
  TableRow,
  TableHead,
  TableCell,
} from '@innostes/ui';

export function SimpleSchedule() {
  return (
    <Table>
      <TableHeader>
        <TableRow>
          <TableHead>Delivery slot</TableHead>
          <TableHead>Driver name</TableHead>
          <TableHead>Vehicle number</TableHead>
        </TableRow>
      </TableHeader>
      <TableBody>
        <TableRow>
          <TableCell>Morning (08:00 - 12:00)</TableCell>
          <TableCell>Ramesh Kumar</TableCell>
          <TableCell className="font-mono">KA-01-MJ-4021</TableCell>
        </TableRow>
      </TableBody>
    </Table>
  );
}
```

### Number and currency alignment

Numerical figures, quantities, and currency amounts should align to the right (`className="text-end"`). Pair with `tabular-nums` or `font-mono` to ensure numerals align consistently along decimal places.

```tsx
import {
  Table,
  TableHeader,
  TableBody,
  TableRow,
  TableHead,
  TableCell,
} from '@innostes/ui';

export function TaxBreakdown() {
  return (
    <Table>
      <TableHeader>
        <TableRow>
          <TableHead>Tax type</TableHead>
          <TableHead className="text-end">Rate</TableHead>
          <TableHead className="text-end">Amount</TableHead>
        </TableRow>
      </TableHeader>
      <TableBody>
        <TableRow>
          <TableCell>CGST (9%)</TableCell>
          <TableCell className="text-end tabular-nums">9.00%</TableCell>
          <TableCell className="text-end font-mono">₹12,780.00</TableCell>
        </TableRow>
        <TableRow>
          <TableCell>SGST (9%)</TableCell>
          <TableCell className="text-end tabular-nums">9.00%</TableCell>
          <TableCell className="text-end font-mono">₹12,780.00</TableCell>
        </TableRow>
      </TableBody>
    </Table>
  );
}
```

### Row selection highlighting

Set `data-state="selected"` on a `TableRow` to apply design-token selection styling (`bg-muted`).

```tsx
import { Table, TableBody, TableRow, TableCell } from '@innostes/ui';

export function HighlightedRow() {
  return (
    <Table>
      <TableBody>
        <TableRow data-state="selected">
          <TableCell className="font-medium">Active ledger entry</TableCell>
          <TableCell>Reconciled</TableCell>
        </TableRow>
      </TableBody>
    </Table>
  );
}
```

### Table captions and footer summaries

Include `TableCaption` to provide accessible context and `TableFooter` for aggregate summary rows.

```tsx
import {
  Table,
  TableHeader,
  TableBody,
  TableFooter,
  TableRow,
  TableHead,
  TableCell,
  TableCaption,
} from '@innostes/ui';

export function AccountSummary() {
  return (
    <Table>
      <TableCaption>Quarterly freight expenses summary</TableCaption>
      <TableHeader>
        <TableRow>
          <TableHead>Month</TableHead>
          <TableHead className="text-end">Dispatches</TableHead>
          <TableHead className="text-end">Freight total</TableHead>
        </TableRow>
      </TableHeader>
      <TableBody>
        <TableRow>
          <TableCell>April 2026</TableCell>
          <TableCell className="text-end tabular-nums">142</TableCell>
          <TableCell className="text-end font-mono">₹4,28,000</TableCell>
        </TableRow>
      </TableBody>
      <TableFooter>
        <TableRow>
          <TableCell>Total</TableCell>
          <TableCell className="text-end tabular-nums">142</TableCell>
          <TableCell className="text-end font-mono">₹4,28,000</TableCell>
        </TableRow>
      </TableFooter>
    </Table>
  );
}
```

## Accessibility

`Table` uses semantic HTML5 elements that assistive technologies recognize natively without additional ARIA roles.

### Semantic markup

- The parent wrapper automatically introduces `overflow-x-auto` to allow horizontal scrolling on smaller screens without clipping content.
- `TableHeader` renders a native `<thead>` and `TableHead` renders `<th>` with appropriate header cell semantics.
- `TableCaption` renders a native `<caption>` element, announcing the table's purpose to screen readers upon focus.

### Screen readers

Assistive technologies announce row and column counts automatically. When navigating through cells, screen readers announce the corresponding column header associated with the cell.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Use Table for static or simple breakdowns (under 20 rows) where custom cell layout and footers are needed.',
    code: `<Table>\n  <TableHeader>...</TableHeader>\n  <TableBody>...</TableBody>\n</Table>`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not re-implement sorting, filtering, and pagination from scratch with Table; use DataTable instead.',
    code: `// Anti-pattern: Hand-rolling complex pagination with raw Table\n<Table>{manualSortedRows.map(...)}</Table>`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Always align numerical values to the right (className="text-end") and use tabular-nums.',
    code: `<TableCell className="text-end tabular-nums">₹4,500.00</TableCell>`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not left-align currency figures or numerical quantities.',
    code: `<TableCell>₹4,500.00</TableCell>`,
  }}
/>

## API reference

<ApiTable
  components={[
    'Table',
    'TableHeader',
    'TableBody',
    'TableFooter',
    'TableRow',
    'TableHead',
    'TableCell',
    'TableCaption',
  ]}
/>

## Related

- [Data Table](/ui/docs/components/data-display/data-table) — Full-featured data grid with sorting, selection, and pagination.
- [Card](/ui/docs/components/data-display/card) — Grouped container for structured content.
- [Badge](/ui/docs/components/data-display/badge) — Status indicators and tags.

## Tree View (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/data-display/tree-view)

Nested tree structure featuring roving focus keyboard navigation, type-ahead search, expandable child levels, and loading spinners.

<ComponentPreview name="data-display/tree-view/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import {
  TreeView,
  type TreeNode,
  type TreeViewProps,
  type TreeViewSlot,
} from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `TreeView` to present deeply nested, hierarchical structures where users navigate between parent categories and child entities:

- Displaying general ledger Chart of Accounts (Assets > Current Assets > Bank Accounts).
- Navigating organizational structures (Departments > Divisions > Regional Teams).
- Browsing product catalogue taxonomy (Electronics > Industrial Automation > Sensors).
- Exploring multi-level warehouse bin and racking locations.

When choosing hierarchical components:
- Use `TreeView` when the hierarchy contains multiple levels and operators need to expand and collapse branches selectively.
- Use [Breadcrumb](/ui/docs/components/navigation/breadcrumb) to show an operator their current position within a linear ancestral hierarchy.
- Use [Accordion](/ui/docs/components/navigation/accordion) when presenting stacked sections of content that expand to reveal detailed panels.

## Examples

### Basic hierarchy

Construct a tree by passing an array of `TreeNode` objects to `items`. Any node with a `children` property is treated as a branch node and displays a collapsible chevron toggle.

```tsx
'use client';

import { useState } from 'react';
import { TreeView, type TreeNode } from '@innostes/ui';

const accounts: TreeNode[] = [
  {
    id: 'assets',
    label: 'Current assets',
    children: [
      { id: 'bank-hdfc', label: 'HDFC Operating Account' },
      { id: 'bank-sbi', label: 'SBI Forex Treasury' },
    ],
  },
  {
    id: 'liabilities',
    label: 'Current liabilities',
    children: [
      { id: 'ap-domestic', label: 'Domestic Trade Payables' },
      { id: 'tax-gst', label: 'GST Output Liability' },
    ],
  },
];

export function ChartOfAccounts() {
  const [selected, setSelected] = useState<string | null>('bank-hdfc');

  return (
    <TreeView
      aria-label="Chart of accounts"
      items={accounts}
      defaultExpanded={['assets']}
      selected={selected}
      onSelectedChange={setSelected}
    />
  );
}
```

### Asynchronous node loading

To load child nodes on demand (e.g. from a backend API when a warehouse zone is clicked), set `loading={true}` on the parent node while the network request is in flight. A spinner automatically displays in place of the chevron toggle.

```tsx
'use client';

import { useState } from 'react';
import { TreeView, type TreeNode } from '@innostes/ui';

export function LazyWarehouseTree() {
  const [items, setItems] = useState<TreeNode[]>([
    { id: 'blr', label: 'Bengaluru Logistics Center', children: [] },
  ]);

  const handleExpandedChange = async (expandedIds: string[]) => {
    if (expandedIds.includes('blr')) {
      // Mark node as loading
      setItems((prev) =>
        prev.map((n) => (n.id === 'blr' ? { ...n, loading: true } : n))
      );

      // Simulate remote fetch
      const bins = await fetch('/api/v1/warehouses/blr/bins').then((r) => r.json());

      setItems((prev) =>
        prev.map((n) =>
          n.id === 'blr' ? { ...n, loading: false, children: bins } : n
        )
      );
    }
  };

  return (
    <TreeView
      aria-label="Warehouse storage tree"
      items={items}
      onExpandedChange={handleExpandedChange}
    />
  );
}
```

### Icons and metadata badges

Enhance nodes by providing leading `icon` elements and trailing `meta` content (such as item counts or currency totals):

```tsx
import { Badge, TreeView, type TreeNode } from '@innostes/ui';
import { Folder, FolderTree } from 'lucide-react';

const catalog: TreeNode[] = [
  {
    id: 'packaging',
    label: 'Packaging materials',
    icon: <FolderTree className="size-4" />,
    meta: <Badge size="sm" variant="secondary">48 SKUs</Badge>,
    children: [
      {
        id: 'corrugated',
        label: 'Corrugated boxes',
        icon: <Folder className="size-4" />,
        meta: <span className="font-mono text-xs text-muted-foreground">₹1,42,000</span>,
      },
    ],
  },
];

export function CatalogTree() {
  return <TreeView aria-label="Inventory catalog" items={catalog} />;
}
```

### Compact sizing

Set `size="sm"` to reduce row height (from 36px to 28px) and font size, making the tree suitable for narrow sidebars and dense file tree palettes.

```tsx
import { TreeView } from '@innostes/ui';

export function DenseTree() {
  return (
    <TreeView
      aria-label="Compact project tree"
      items={accounts}
      size="sm"
    />
  );
}
```

## Accessibility

`TreeView` strictly adheres to the W3C WAI-ARIA Treeview Design Pattern.

### Keyboard navigation

<KeyboardTable
  entries={[
    { key: 'Up Arrow / Down Arrow', action: 'Moves focus to the previous or next visible node in the tree.' },
    { key: 'Right Arrow', action: 'Expands a collapsed branch node, or moves focus to the first child of an expanded branch.' },
    { key: 'Left Arrow', action: 'Collapses an expanded branch node, or moves focus up to the parent node.' },
    { key: 'Home / End', action: 'Moves focus to the first or last visible node in the entire tree.' },
    { key: 'Enter / Space', action: 'Selects the currently focused node.' },
    { key: 'Character keys', action: 'Type-ahead search jumps focus to the next node starting with the typed letter.' },
  ]}
/>

### Screen readers and tree semantics

- The root element uses `role="tree"` with `aria-label` defining the tree's purpose.
- Each branch node has `role="treeitem"`, carrying `aria-expanded="true"` or `aria-expanded="false"`, along with `aria-level` denoting depth in the hierarchy.
- The tree represents a single tab stop with roving tabindex across nodes.
- When `loading={true}`, the node announces the `loadingLabel` ("Loading…" by default) to assistive technologies.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Ensure every TreeNode has a globally unique, stable id attribute (e.g. database UUID or slug).',
    code: `{ id: 'dept-finance', label: 'Finance' }`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not generate random or index-based IDs on every render; this breaks keyboard focus tracking.',
    code: `{ id: Math.random().toString(), label: 'Finance' } // Causes focus loss`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Use the textValue prop if label contains complex JSX, ensuring type-ahead search functions properly.',
    code: `{ id: 'tax', label: <span>GST (18%)</span>, textValue: 'GST' }`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not omit textValue when passing custom JSX labels; type-ahead keyboard navigation will fail.',
    code: `{ id: 'tax', label: <CustomBadge>GST</CustomBadge> }`,
  }}
/>

## API reference

<ApiTable components={['TreeView']} />

## Related

- [Accordion](/ui/docs/components/navigation/accordion) — Vertically stacked collapsible panels.
- [Breadcrumb](/ui/docs/components/navigation/breadcrumb) — Linear ancestral navigation path.
- [Data Table](/ui/docs/components/data-display/data-table) — Tabular presentation for flat datasets.

## Alert (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/feedback/alert)

In-flow status callout with semantic variants, automatic ARIA role management (alert vs status), and integrated iconography.

<ComponentPreview name="feedback/alert/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import {
  Alert,
  AlertTitle,
  AlertDescription,
  type AlertProps,
} from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `Alert` when an important message requires persistent visibility in the page flow directly above relevant content:

- Announcing planned server maintenance, downtime windows, or fiscal year cutoff dates.
- Displaying critical prerequisite warnings before an irreversible action (e.g. "GST e-invoicing portal offline").
- Warning operators about section-level configuration errors or unverified business credentials.

When choosing feedback mechanisms:
- Use `Alert` for persistent, non-modal notices that should stay visible until resolved or dismissed.
- Use [Toast](/ui/docs/components/feedback/toast) for transient confirmations that automatically disappear after a few seconds.
- Use [Field error](/ui/docs/components/forms/field) when an issue belongs directly to a single form input.
- Refer to the [Feedback decision guide](/ui/docs/components/feedback#feedback-decision-guide) for an overview of all feedback channels.

## Examples

### Semantic variants

`Alert` provides four semantic variants: `info`, `success`, `warning`, and `destructive`. Each variant renders an appropriate default icon and sets semantic border and background tints.

```tsx
import { Alert, AlertTitle, AlertDescription } from '@innostes/ui';

export function MaintenanceAlert() {
  return (
    <Alert variant="warning">
      <AlertTitle>Tax filing deadline approaching</AlertTitle>
      <AlertDescription>
        GSTR-1 filing for the month of September must be completed by 11 October 2026.
      </AlertDescription>
    </Alert>
  );
}
```

### Custom icon and titleless alerts

Pass a custom React node to `icon` to override the default variant icon, or pass `icon={null}` to omit the icon entirely. Alerts can also render simple text without an explicit `AlertTitle`:

```tsx
import { Alert, AlertDescription } from '@innostes/ui';
import { ShieldCheck } from 'lucide-react';

export function VerifiedAlert() {
  return (
    <Alert variant="success" icon={<ShieldCheck />}>
      <AlertDescription>
        Vendor bank account verified via penny-drop validation.
      </AlertDescription>
    </Alert>
  );
}
```

### Form warning integration

Place an `Alert` directly above form fields to explain global prerequisites or non-field constraints:

```tsx
import { Alert, AlertTitle, AlertDescription, Field, Input, Label } from '@innostes/ui';

export function PurchaseOrderForm() {
  return (
    <form className="flex flex-col gap-4">
      <Alert variant="info">
        <AlertTitle>Exchange rate notice</AlertTitle>
        <AlertDescription>
          International purchase orders will lock currency conversions at RBI benchmark rates upon submission.
        </AlertDescription>
      </Alert>

      <Field>
        <Label htmlFor="vendor">Vendor name</Label>
        <Input id="vendor" defaultValue="Tata Consumer Products" />
      </Field>
    </form>
  );
}
```

### Inline action links

Include action links or buttons within `AlertDescription` to provide direct recovery paths:

```tsx
import { Alert, AlertTitle, AlertDescription, Button } from '@innostes/ui';

export function QuotaAlert() {
  return (
    <Alert variant="warning">
      <AlertTitle>Warehouse storage quota</AlertTitle>
      <AlertDescription className="flex items-center justify-between">
        <span>Depot capacity has reached 92%. Allocate additional space to continue receiving pallets.</span>
        <Button size="sm" variant="outline" className="shrink-0 ml-4">
          Request expansion
        </Button>
      </AlertDescription>
    </Alert>
  );
}
```

## Accessibility

`Alert` automatically manages ARIA live regions and accessibility roles based on the selected variant.

### Live regions and ARIA roles

- For `variant="destructive"` and `variant="warning"`, `Alert` automatically sets `role="alert"`. This instructs assistive technologies to announce the message immediately (assertive live region), interrupting other speech.
- For `variant="default"`, `variant="info"`, and `variant="success"`, `Alert` sets `role="status"`. This announces the message politely once the user finishes their current reading stream.
- Icons are rendered with `aria-hidden="true"` to prevent screen readers from announcing decorative icon names.

### Screen readers

- When alerts mount dynamically (e.g. after a form submission or failed API call), placing them in the DOM triggers automatic screen reader announcement.
- Avoid updating alert contents continuously in real time to prevent confusing audio chatter for screen reader users.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Use Alert for persistent section or page notices that require user awareness before proceeding.',
    code: `<Alert variant="warning"><AlertTitle>Account unverified</AlertTitle></Alert>`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not use Alert for short-lived operation confirmations like "Item saved" (use Toast instead).',
    code: `<Alert variant="success"><AlertTitle>Saved!</AlertTitle></Alert> // Clutters layout permanently`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Include an actionable recovery step or explanatory description alongside the title.',
    code: `<Alert variant="destructive">\n  <AlertTitle>Payment failed</AlertTitle>\n  <AlertDescription>Update your billing card in settings.</AlertDescription>\n</Alert>`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not post vague alerts that explain an error occurred without explaining how to fix it.',
    code: `<Alert variant="destructive"><AlertTitle>Error 500</AlertTitle></Alert>`,
  }}
/>

## API reference

<ApiTable components={['Alert', 'AlertTitle', 'AlertDescription']} />

## Related

- [Toast](/ui/docs/components/feedback/toast) — Transient notifications that auto-dismiss.
- [Field](/ui/docs/components/forms/field) — Form field container with inline error messages.
- [Alert Dialog](/ui/docs/components/overlays/alert-dialog) — Modal dialog for critical confirmation prompts.

## Gauge (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/feedback/gauge)

Accessible SVG radial meter with dynamic threshold coloring, customizable radius dimensions, and normalized range calculations.

<ComponentPreview name="feedback/gauge/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import { Gauge, type GaugeProps, type GaugeTone, type GaugeSlot } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `Gauge` when an executive dashboard requires a circular dial to communicate an operational metric, utilization rate, or SLA compliance score:

- Showing warehouse storage capacity utilization or truck fleet availability.
- Displaying SLA fulfillment percentages or customer satisfaction ratings.
- Visualizing annual budget expenditure versus fiscal limits.

When choosing scalar components:
- Use `Gauge` for prominent, radial visual dials on operational and executive dashboards.
- Use [Meter](/ui/docs/components/feedback/meter) for compact, linear horizontal bars in dense tables or cards.
- Use [Progress](/ui/docs/components/feedback/progress) for active workflows or tasks advancing toward completion.
- Refer to the [Feedback decision guide](/ui/docs/components/feedback#feedback-decision-guide) for full guidance.

## Examples

### Basic radial dial

Provide `value`, `min`, `max`, and a descriptive `label`:

```tsx
import { Gauge } from '@innostes/ui';

export function DispatchGauge() {
  return (
    <Gauge
      value={84}
      max={100}
      label="Daily dispatch target"
      description="840 of 1,000 pallets loaded"
      format={{ style: 'percent' }}
    />
  );
}
```

### Dynamic threshold coloring

Pass a function to `tone` to change the arc color dynamically as the measured metric enters warning or critical bands:

```tsx
import { Gauge } from '@innostes/ui';

const computeTone = (val: number) => {
  if (val > 90) return 'destructive';
  if (val > 75) return 'warning';
  return 'success';
};

export function StorageGauge() {
  return (
    <Gauge
      value={92}
      max={100}
      label="Cold storage utilization"
      description="Zone B Freezers"
      tone={computeTone}
    />
  );
}
```

### Metric descriptions and sizing

Control the overall dial width using `size` (e.g. `'12rem'` or `200`). Add a secondary `description` under the label:

```tsx
import { Gauge } from '@innostes/ui';

export function SlaComplianceGauge() {
  return (
    <Gauge
      value={99.2}
      max={100}
      size="12rem"
      label="Order delivery SLA"
      description="Last 30 days rolling"
      format={{ style: 'percent', maximumFractionDigits: 1 }}
      tone="success"
    />
  );
}
```

## Accessibility

`Gauge` wraps Base UI Meter primitives (`@base-ui/react/meter`).

### Screen readers and meter semantics

- Renders with `role="meter"` and sets `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, and `aria-valuemax`.
- The `label` prop is connected to the meter as its accessible name.
- Percentage calculations are normalized against the span between `min` and `max` so screen readers announce human-readable fractions (e.g., "Daily dispatch target, 84%").
- The SVG arc elements include `aria-hidden="true"`, ensuring assistive technologies rely exclusively on the semantic meter attributes.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Use a dynamic tone function to clearly differentiate normal, warning, and critical operating thresholds.',
    code: `<Gauge tone={(v) => (v > 90 ? 'destructive' : 'primary')} />`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not render gauges with uniform coloring when the metric represents an urgent threshold limit.',
    code: `<Gauge value={98} max={100} tone="primary" /> // Fails to signal critical threshold`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Always provide a clear label and description so operators understand what the dial measures.',
    code: `<Gauge value={78} label="Fleet active" description="78 of 100 trucks in transit" />`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not present isolated numeric percentages without clarifying the measured dimension.',
    code: `<Gauge value={78} /> // Unlabeled dial`,
  }}
/>

## API reference

<ApiTable components={['Gauge']} baseUi="meter" />

## Related

- [Meter](/ui/docs/components/feedback/meter) — Linear horizontal measurement bar.
- [Progress](/ui/docs/components/feedback/progress) — Task advancement indicator for uploads and jobs.
- [Stat](/ui/docs/components/data-display/stat) — Metric display card with trends.

## Feedback (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/feedback/index)

Decision guides, severity wording principles, and UI components for communicating system status, background tasks, and operation outcomes.

import { CategoryGrid } from '@/components/docs/category-grid';

# Feedback

Feedback components inform operators at Northwind Traders Pvt Ltd about system status, background processes, verification failures, and operation outcomes. Choosing the correct communication pattern prevents alert fatigue while ensuring critical errors are never overlooked.

## Components

<CategoryGrid category="components/feedback" />

## Feedback decision guide

Use this decision matrix to determine which feedback mechanism matches your application scenario:

| Mechanism | Placement | Persistence | Interruption level | Ideal use case |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **[Toast](/ui/docs/components/feedback/toast)** | Floating viewport corner | Transient (auto-dismiss 4–6s) | Non-blocking | Success confirmations ("Invoice INV-8402 created"), non-critical updates. |
| **[Alert](/ui/docs/components/feedback/alert)** | In-page banner directly above content | Persistent until resolved or dismissed | Non-blocking | Section-level notices, scheduled maintenance warnings, fiscal year closing notices. |
| **[Field error](/ui/docs/components/forms/field)** | Directly underneath the invalid input | Persistent until input value changes | Focused | Form validation errors (invalid GSTIN, missing PO line item, overdue date). |
| **[EmptyState](/ui/docs/components/data-display/empty-state)** | Replacing empty lists or tables | Persistent | Contextual | Zero results, blank initial modules, cleared queues. |
| **[Alert Dialog](/ui/docs/components/overlays/alert-dialog)** | Centered modal overlay | Blocking modal dialog | Disruptive modal | Irreversible actions requiring explicit confirmation (deleting a vendor, voiding a fiscal ledger). |

## Severity wording guidelines

Match the severity tone to the true operational consequence:

### Informational (`info`)
- **Tone**: Neutral, informative, helpful.
- **Guidance**: Explain background events or helpful workflow hints that require no immediate action.
- **Example**: *"GST e-invoicing portal auto-sync is scheduled for 11:00 PM IST."*

### Success (`success`)
- **Tone**: Positive, succinct, affirming.
- **Guidance**: Confirm that the user's action completed successfully. State what was achieved.
- **Example**: *"Purchase order PO-8410 approved and dispatched to vendor."*

### Warning (`warning`)
- **Tone**: Cautionary, proactive, advisory.
- **Guidance**: Alert the user to a non-blocking condition that may cause failure if ignored. State the consequence.
- **Example**: *"Warehouse bin B-12 is at 94% capacity. Additional stock receipts may require re-routing."*

### Destructive / Error (`destructive`)
- **Tone**: Clear, calm, actionable. Never blame the user.
- **Guidance**: Explain plainly what failed, why it failed, and how the user can resolve the issue. Avoid cryptic error codes.
- **Example**: *"Unable to reconcile bank statement. The transaction date falls outside the active accounting period."*

## Progress versus meter versus gauge

The design system provides three distinct scalar indicators:

1. **[Progress](/ui/docs/components/feedback/progress)** (`role="progressbar"`):
   - Indicates **task completion** or workflow transition over time.
   - Example: Uploading vendor attachments, compiling monthly GST reports, processing batch invoice PDFs.
2. **[Meter](/ui/docs/components/feedback/meter)** (`role="meter"`):
   - Measures a **scalar value within a fixed range** where the quantity represents an existing measurement rather than progress toward a goal.
   - Example: Storage disk quota utilized, memory footprint, cold-room warehouse temperature.
3. **[Gauge](/ui/docs/components/feedback/gauge)**:
   - A **radial visual meter** with customizable threshold zones (normal, warning, critical) for operational dashboards.
   - Example: Fleet delivery on-time performance, server health score, SLA compliance percentage.

---

## Meter (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/feedback/meter)

Scalar measurement indicator with semantic tones, normalized percent calculations, and full WAI-ARIA meter semantics.

<ComponentPreview name="feedback/meter/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import { Meter, type MeterProps } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `Meter` to communicate an existing scalar measurement or capacity against known numerical bounds:

- Displaying storage consumption, memory usage, or compute quotas.
- Tracking organization seat license utilization (e.g. 8 of 10 operator licenses used).
- Monitoring warehouse bin volume or tank fuel levels.

When choosing scalar components:
- Use `Meter` (`role="meter"`) for static capacity or volume measurements within a fixed range.
- Use [Progress](/ui/docs/components/feedback/progress) (`role="progressbar"`) when an active task is advancing toward completion.
- Use [Gauge](/ui/docs/components/feedback/gauge) when you need an executive radial dial display on KPI dashboards.
- Refer to the [Feedback decision guide](/ui/docs/components/feedback#feedback-decision-guide) for guidance on all feedback mechanisms.

## Examples

### Basic capacity measurement

Provide `value`, `min`, `max`, and a descriptive `label`:

```tsx
import { Meter } from '@innostes/ui';

export function StorageMeter() {
  return (
    <Meter
      value={64}
      max={100}
      label="Cloud document storage"
      format={{ style: 'unit', unit: 'gigabyte' }}
    />
  );
}
```

### Warning and destructive tones

Set `tone` to `primary`, `success`, `warning`, or `destructive` to communicate status severity as a metric approaches full capacity:

```tsx
import { Meter } from '@innostes/ui';

export function CapacityTones() {
  const usedSeats = 9;
  const maxSeats = 10;
  const isCritical = usedSeats / maxSeats > 0.85;

  return (
    <Meter
      value={usedSeats}
      max={maxSeats}
      label="Dispatch operator licenses"
      tone={isCritical ? 'destructive' : 'primary'}
      showValue
    />
  );
}
```

### Normalized percentage formatting

When `format={{ style: 'percent' }}` is specified, `Meter` normalizes `value` against `min` and `max` so that `value={72}` with `max={100}` renders `"72%"` (rather than `"7,200%"`):

```tsx
import { Meter } from '@innostes/ui';

export function NormalizedQuotaMeter() {
  return (
    <Meter
      value={84}
      min={0}
      max={100}
      label="Monthly API rate limit"
      format={{ style: 'percent' }}
      tone="warning"
    />
  );
}
```

## Accessibility

`Meter` is built on Base UI Meter primitives (`@base-ui/react/meter`).

### Screen readers and meter semantics

- Renders with native `role="meter"`.
- Sets `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, and `aria-valuemax` automatically.
- Screen readers announce the current reading in relation to the upper and lower boundaries (e.g., "Cloud document storage, 64 gigabytes, 64%").
- When `format={{ style: 'percent' }}` is used, `aria-valuetext` announces the correct computed percentage string.

### Color independence

Avoid relying strictly on the bar color to communicate limit risks. Always provide clear numerical text or helper copy indicating proximity to the maximum capacity.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Use Meter for scalar measurements (such as memory, disk storage, or budget consumed).',
    code: `<Meter value={45} max={100} label="Storage" />`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not use Meter to indicate file download or data export progress (use Progress instead).',
    code: `// Semantically incorrect: Download is a task advancing in time\n<Meter value={downloadedBytes} label="Downloading" />`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Switch tone to "warning" or "destructive" dynamically when usage approaches 80% or 95% capacity.',
    code: `<Meter value={used} max={max} tone={used / max > 0.9 ? 'destructive' : 'primary'} />`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not leave critical quota overflow states styled in neutral primary blue without visual distinction.',
    code: `<Meter value={99} max={100} tone="primary" />`,
  }}
/>

## API reference

<ApiTable components={['Meter']} baseUi="meter" />

## Related

- [Progress](/ui/docs/components/feedback/progress) — Task advancement indicator for uploads and jobs.
- [Gauge](/ui/docs/components/feedback/gauge) — Radial dial gauge for operational dashboards.
- [Stat](/ui/docs/components/data-display/stat) — Metric display card with trends.

## Progress (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/feedback/progress)

Accessible progress indicator supporting determinate progress, indeterminate pulse animations, and normalized percent formatting.

<ComponentPreview name="feedback/progress/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import { Progress, type ProgressProps } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `Progress` to visualize task advancement toward completion over time:

- Tracking multi-file uploads or bulk CSV imports.
- Displaying batch background processing (e.g. generating monthly GST e-invoices).
- Indicating indeterminate loading when the total duration cannot be predicted.

When choosing between scalar indicators:
- Use `Progress` (`role="progressbar"`) when tracking an active task advancing toward completion over time.
- Use [Meter](/ui/docs/components/feedback/meter) (`role="meter"`) when measuring an existing static scalar value in a fixed range (such as storage capacity, memory usage, or user seat licenses).
- Use [Gauge](/ui/docs/components/feedback/gauge) when displaying an executive radial dial on operational KPI dashboards.
- Refer to the [Feedback decision guide](/ui/docs/components/feedback#feedback-decision-guide) for full details.

## Examples

### Determinate task progress

Supply `value`, `min`, `max`, and a descriptive `label`. Enable `showValue={true}` to render the formatted numerical value or percentage alongside the label:

```tsx
'use client';

import { useState, useEffect } from 'react';
import { Progress } from '@innostes/ui';

export function DocumentUploadProgress() {
  const [percent, setPercent] = useState(45);

  return (
    <Progress
      value={percent}
      label="Uploading consignment manifests"
      format={{ style: 'percent' }}
      showValue
    />
  );
}
```

### Indeterminate loading state

When background task duration or payload size is unknown, pass `value={null}`. The component renders an animated sweeping pulse across the track:

```tsx
import { Progress } from '@innostes/ui';

export function IndeterminateReportProgress() {
  return (
    <Progress
      value={null}
      label="Compiling quarterly GST reconciliation…"
      aria-label="Compiling GST report"
    />
  );
}
```

### Custom value formatting

Pass `Intl.NumberFormatOptions` via the `format` prop to format units such as bytes, files, or custom numbers:

```tsx
import { Progress } from '@innostes/ui';

export function BatchExportProgress() {
  return (
    <Progress
      value={142}
      max={500}
      label="Processed purchase orders"
      format={{ style: 'decimal' }}
      showValue
    />
  );
}
```

## Accessibility

`Progress` wraps Base UI Progress primitives (`@base-ui/react/progress`).

### Screen readers and progressbar semantics

- The element carries `role="progressbar"`.
- When determinate (`value != null`), `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, and `aria-valuemax` are maintained automatically.
- When `format={{ style: 'percent' }}` is passed, `Progress` computes the percentage fraction relative to `min` and `max`, ensuring `value={45}` out of `100` announces "45%" to screen readers rather than "4,500%".
- Indeterminate state removes `aria-valuenow`, signaling to assistive technologies that progress is active without a known percentage.

### Reduced motion

When the user specifies `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` in system settings, `Progress` disables continuous animations on the indeterminate track and suppresses width transitions.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Use Progress for active tasks advancing toward completion (such as file uploads or batch exports).',
    code: `<Progress value={transferred} max={totalBytes} label="Uploading" />`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not use Progress to display static capacity or remaining quota measurements (use Meter instead).',
    code: `// Semantically incorrect: Quota is a scalar measurement, not a task in progress\n<Progress value={storageUsed} max={storageQuota} label="Disk usage" />`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Always provide an explicit label prop or aria-label attribute explaining what task is in progress.',
    code: `<Progress value={65} label="Generating invoices" />`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not render a bare progress bar without accessible naming.',
    code: `<Progress value={65} /> // Unlabeled progress bar`,
  }}
/>

## API reference

<ApiTable components={['Progress']} baseUi="progress" />

## Related

- [Meter](/ui/docs/components/feedback/meter) — Linear bar for scalar capacity and quota measurements.
- [Gauge](/ui/docs/components/feedback/gauge) — Radial dial gauge for operational dashboard KPIs.
- [Spinner](/ui/docs/components/feedback/spinner) — Compact circular loading indicator.

## Skeleton (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/feedback/skeleton)

Accessible content loading placeholder that prevents Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) and respects reduced motion preferences.

<ComponentPreview name="feedback/skeleton/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import { Skeleton } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `Skeleton` to provide a low-contrast visual preview of content geometry while asynchronous data fetches are in flight:

- Mirroring cards, user profiles, or dashboard tiles on initial page load.
- Rendering placeholder rows in [DataTable](/ui/docs/components/data-display/data-table) or lists during search queries.
- Preventing Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) as images, fonts, and API payloads hydrate into view.

When choosing loading representations:
- Use `Skeleton` when you know the approximate dimensions of the incoming layout structure (cards, tables, lists).
- Use [Spinner](/ui/docs/components/feedback/spinner) inside action buttons or compact controls during quick submission operations (< 1s).
- Use [Progress](/ui/docs/components/feedback/progress) when tracking a background upload or multi-step batch job.

## Examples

### Basic card placeholder

Size `Skeleton` components using standard Tailwind width and height utilities to match the expected content proportions:

```tsx
import { Skeleton } from '@innostes/ui';

export function ProfileCardSkeleton() {
  return (
    <div
      aria-busy="true"
      aria-label="Loading vendor profile"
      className="flex flex-col gap-4 rounded-xl border p-6"
    >
      <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
        <Skeleton className="size-12 rounded-full" />
        <div className="flex flex-1 flex-col gap-2">
          <Skeleton className="h-4 w-1/3" />
          <Skeleton className="h-3 w-1/4" />
        </div>
      </div>
      <Skeleton className="h-20 w-full" />
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Table row skeletons

Render multiple skeleton rows to indicate that a data table is actively fetching its next page:

```tsx
import { Skeleton } from '@innostes/ui';

export function TableLoadingRows() {
  return (
    <div aria-busy="true" className="flex flex-col gap-3">
      {Array.from({ length: 4 }).map((_, i) => (
        <div key={i} className="flex items-center justify-between gap-4 py-2 border-b">
          <Skeleton className="h-4 w-28" />
          <Skeleton className="h-4 w-48" />
          <Skeleton className="h-4 w-16" />
          <Skeleton className="h-4 w-20" />
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Layout shift prevention

Mirror typography heights (`h-4` for `text-sm`, `h-5` for `text-base`, `h-8` for `text-2xl`) so the layout remains steady when real content mounts:

```tsx
import { Skeleton } from '@innostes/ui';

export function StatTileSkeleton() {
  return (
    <div aria-busy="true" className="flex flex-col gap-2 rounded-xl border p-5">
      <Skeleton className="h-4 w-24" />
      <Skeleton className="h-8 w-32" />
      <Skeleton className="h-3 w-40" />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Accessibility

`Skeleton` is carefully designed to avoid distracting screen reader chatter during network fetches.

### Container aria-busy and aria-live

- `Skeleton` elements are marked with `aria-hidden="true"`, ensuring assistive technologies do not announce every individual placeholder bar.
- Always add `aria-busy="true"` and an `aria-label` (e.g. `aria-label="Loading purchase orders"`) on the parent container enclosing the skeletons. Remove `aria-busy` once real data has populated the DOM.

### Reduced motion support

When a user enables `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` in their operating system accessibility settings, the pulsing animation is automatically disabled (`motion-reduce:animate-none`), displaying a steady muted background.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Match the approximate height and border radius of the real component to prevent layout jumping.',
    code: `<Skeleton className="h-10 w-full rounded-md" /> // Matches Button or Input`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not render generic fixed-size rectangles that differ significantly from the hydrated content shape.',
    code: `<Skeleton className="h-40 w-40" /> // In an inline text field`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Apply aria-busy="true" to the parent landmark or container holding the skeletons.',
    code: `<div aria-busy="true" aria-label="Loading orders"><Skeleton ... /></div>`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not omit aria-busy on the loading container, leaving screen reader users unaware that data is in flight.',
    code: `<div><Skeleton ... /></div>`,
  }}
/>

## API reference

<ApiTable components={['Skeleton']} />

## Related

- [Spinner](/ui/docs/components/feedback/spinner) — Circular spinner for inline buttons and compact loading states.
- [Progress](/ui/docs/components/feedback/progress) — Linear progress bar for known percentages.
- [Data Table](/ui/docs/components/data-display/data-table) — Data grid with built-in skeleton loading rows.

## Spinner (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/feedback/spinner)

Circular loading glyph with automatic aria-status management, size utilities, and decorative hiding toggles.

<ComponentPreview name="feedback/spinner/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import { Spinner, type SpinnerProps } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `Spinner` to indicate localized asynchronous activity when space does not permit a full skeleton or progress bar:

- Indicating asynchronous background sync in table headers or stat cards.
- Rendering an inline indicator next to a "Saving draft…" status note.
- Showing loading spinners in asynchronous dropdown search results.

When choosing loading components:
- Use `Spinner` for compact inline loading indicators and isolated status chips.
- Use `Button loading` directly on buttons rather than nesting a manual `<Spinner />` inside the button label.
- Use [Skeleton](/ui/docs/components/feedback/skeleton) when fetching initial page layouts or table records.
- Use [Progress](/ui/docs/components/feedback/progress) for determinate task progression (uploads, exports).

## Examples

### Basic spinner

By default, `Spinner` renders at `size-4` (16px) and carries an accessible label of `"Loading"` with `role="status"`:

```tsx
import { Spinner } from '@innostes/ui';

export function DefaultSpinner() {
  return <Spinner aria-label="Loading purchase orders" />;
}
```

### Sizing and color inheritance

`Spinner` uses `stroke="currentColor"` so it automatically matches the text color of its parent container. Adjust its dimensions using standard Tailwind `size-*` utilities:

```tsx
import { Spinner } from '@innostes/ui';

export function SizedSpinners() {
  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-4">
      <Spinner className="size-4" />
      <Spinner className="size-6 text-primary" />
      <Spinner className="size-8 text-muted-foreground" />
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Inlined with status text

When a spinner sits directly beside descriptive text (such as "Syncing ledger..."), pass `label={null}`. This marks the spinner as decorative (`aria-hidden="true"`), preventing screen readers from announcing duplicate loading messages:

```tsx
import { Spinner } from '@innostes/ui';

export function InlineStatus() {
  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-2 text-sm text-muted-foreground">
      <Spinner label={null} />
      <span>Reconciling bank transactions…</span>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Inside buttons and controls

For interactive buttons, always prefer the built-in `loading` prop on [Button](/ui/docs/components/actions/button). It automatically manages focus, disables pointer events, and injects a spinner with proper ARIA attributes:

```tsx
import { Button } from '@innostes/ui';

export function SubmitButton({ isSubmitting }: { isSubmitting: boolean }) {
  return (
    <Button loading={isSubmitting} type="submit">
      Approve purchase order
    </Button>
  );
}
```

## Accessibility

`Spinner` handles assistive technology notifications gracefully.

### Accessible labels versus decorative hiding

- When `label` is provided (defaults to `"Loading"`), `Spinner` sets `role="status"` and `aria-label={label}`. Screen readers announce the status update politely.
- When `label={null}` is explicitly passed, `Spinner` removes `role="status"` and sets `aria-hidden="true"`, ensuring no extraneous speech is triggered when accompanying text already explains the state.

### Screen readers and role="status"

- By using `role="status"`, screen readers wait until the current utterance completes before announcing the loading state, preventing jarring speech interruptions.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Set `label={null}` when the spinner is paired with visible explanatory text (e.g. "Syncing...").',
    code: `<span className="flex items-center gap-2"><Spinner label={null} /> Saving…</span>`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not omit `label={null}` next to text; screen readers will announce "Loading Saving…".',
    code: `<span className="flex items-center gap-2"><Spinner /> Saving…</span>`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Use the loading prop on Button rather than manually placing a Spinner inside button children.',
    code: `<Button loading={isSubmitting}>Submit</Button>`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not manually place a bare Spinner inside a button without disabling click events.',
    code: `<Button><Spinner /> Submit</Button> // Allows double-clicks while loading`,
  }}
/>

## API reference

<ApiTable components={['Spinner']} />

## Related

- [Button](/ui/docs/components/actions/button) — Action button with built-in loading spinner support.
- [Skeleton](/ui/docs/components/feedback/skeleton) — Placeholder shapes for incoming content.
- [Progress](/ui/docs/components/feedback/progress) — Linear progress bar for measurable task progression.

## Toast (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/feedback/toast)

Framework-agnostic imperative toast manager with success/error shortcuts, promise resolution tracking, and accessible politeness priority queues.

<ComponentPreview name="feedback/toast/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import {
  toast,
  Toaster,
  type ToastOptions,
  type ToastType,
  type ToasterProps,
} from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `toast` to communicate transient outcomes of user-initiated operations without interrupting workflow:

- Confirming successful record creation, deletion, or archival ("PO-8410 created").
- Providing short-lived "Undo" buttons after bulk batch actions.
- Tracking asynchronous background mutations via `toast.promise`.

When deciding between feedback mechanisms:
- Use `toast` for transient, non-critical confirmations that do not require explicit operator acknowledgement.
- Use [Alert](/ui/docs/components/feedback/alert) for persistent warnings that remain in the page flow until resolved.
- Use [Alert Dialog](/ui/docs/components/overlays/alert-dialog) for high-stakes, irreversible confirmations.
- Refer to the [Feedback decision guide](/ui/docs/components/feedback#feedback-decision-guide) for full guidance.

## Examples

### Toaster configuration

Mount `<Toaster />` once near the root of your application (typically in `layout.tsx` or `App.tsx`):

```tsx
import { Toaster } from '@innostes/ui';

export function RootLayout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <html lang="en">
      <body>
        {children}
        <Toaster position="bottom-right" />
      </body>
    </html>
  );
}
```

### Toast triggers and shortcuts

Call `toast` imperatively from anywhere in your codebase—including asynchronous handlers, store callbacks, or API clients:

```tsx
import { toast } from '@innostes/ui';

// Direct notification
toast('Draft saved automatically');

// Semantic shortcuts
toast.success('Invoice INV-8402 generated');
toast.info('Export queue is processing 42 records');
toast.warning('Warehouse quota exceeds 90%');
toast.error('Failed to sync GSTN data', {
  description: 'Network gateway timed out. Please retry shortly.',
});
```

### Action buttons and undo patterns

Attach an interactive action button to the toast notification by passing the `action` property:

```tsx
import { toast } from '@innostes/ui';

export function archivePurchaseOrder(id: string) {
  // Archive mutation logic...

  toast('Purchase order archived', {
    action: {
      label: 'Undo',
      onClick: () => restorePurchaseOrder(id),
    },
    timeout: 6000,
  });
}
```

### Async promise tracking

Use `toast.promise` to automatically transition a toast through loading, success, and error states as an asynchronous promise resolves:

```tsx
import { toast } from '@innostes/ui';

async function handleSubmitQuotation(quotationData: FormData) {
  await toast.promise(
    fetch('/api/v1/quotations', { method: 'POST', body: quotationData }),
    {
      loading: 'Submitting quotation to procurement portal…',
      success: 'Quotation submitted successfully.',
      error: (err) => `Failed to submit: ${(err as Error).message}`,
    }
  );
}
```

### Updating and dismiss controls

Every toast call returns a unique string identifier. Use `toast.update` to modify an active toast or `toast.dismiss` to close it programmatically:

```tsx
import { toast } from '@innostes/ui';

const toastId = toast.loading('Exporting ledger CSV…');

try {
  await exportLedger();
  toast.update(toastId, {
    type: 'success',
    title: 'Ledger export complete',
    timeout: 4000,
  });
} catch {
  toast.update(toastId, {
    type: 'error',
    title: 'Export interrupted',
    timeout: 5000,
  });
}
```

## Accessibility

`Toast` is built on Base UI Toast primitives (`@base-ui/react/toast`).

### Politeness and ARIA live regions

- Standard notifications (`default`, `info`, `success`) use `priority="low"`, emitting `aria-live="polite"`. The screen reader announces the notification when the user pauses their current interaction.
- Errors (`type="error"`) automatically set `priority="high"`, emitting `aria-live="assertive"`. The screen reader announces error notifications immediately, ensuring operators are alerted to failures.
- Hovering or shifting keyboard focus to the toaster pauses the auto-dismiss timer, allowing users sufficient time to read messages or click actions.

### Focus management and dismiss actions

- Toasts include an accessible close button (`aria-label="Close"`) with keyboard accessibility.
- When an `action` button is present, operators can press `Tab` into the toast region to trigger it without losing their previous document position.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Keep toast messages concise, ideally under 10 words (e.g. "Invoice sent to billing desk").',
    code: `toast.success('Invoice sent to billing desk');`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not place multi-paragraph instructions or technical stack traces inside transient toasts.',
    code: `toast.error('Exception in Thread "main": java.lang.NullPointer...'); // Unreadable in 5s`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Use toast.promise for background mutations to provide instant feedback while saving.',
    code: `toast.promise(save(), { loading: 'Saving...', success: 'Saved', error: 'Failed' });`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not fire successive unlinked toasts that flood the screen with duplicate notifications.',
    code: `// Flood: creates 3 stacked toasts\ntoast('1/3'); toast('2/3'); toast('3/3');`,
  }}
/>

## API reference

<ApiTable components={['Toaster']} baseUi="toast" />

### Imperative toast methods

| Method | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `toast` | `(title, options?) => string` | Dispatches a default toast notification. |
| `toast.success` | `(title, options?) => string` | Dispatches a success toast with checkmark icon. |
| `toast.error` | `(title, options?) => string` | Dispatches an assertive error toast. |
| `toast.warning` | `(title, options?) => string` | Dispatches a warning toast with alert triangle. |
| `toast.info` | `(title, options?) => string` | Dispatches an informational toast. |
| `toast.loading` | `(title, options?) => string` | Dispatches a persistent loading toast with spinner. |
| `toast.update` | `(id, options) => void` | Updates an existing toast's title, description, or type. |
| `toast.dismiss` | `(id?) => void` | Closes a specific toast, or all toasts when called without ID. |
| `toast.promise` | `(promise, messages) => Promise<T>` | Binds toast status to a Promise's lifecycle. |

## Related

- [Alert](/ui/docs/components/feedback/alert) — Persistent banners for non-transient warnings.
- [Spinner](/ui/docs/components/feedback/spinner) — Loading spinners for inline UI elements.
- [Progress](/ui/docs/components/feedback/progress) — Linear progress bar for measurable task completion.

---

## Calendar (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/forms/calendar)

Single and range modes, min/max bounds, disabled dates, one or two month views, and Intl-based locale formatting.

<ComponentPreview name="forms/calendar/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import { Calendar, type DateRange, type Weekday } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

Use `Calendar` when users need to see an inline month view to choose a single calendar day or an inclusive date range:

- Displaying booking schedules, dispatch timetables, or delivery cutoffs directly on an ERP dashboard.
- Selecting ranges across one or two months when visualising calendar context is essential.
- Building custom date filter panels.

When choosing between date selection patterns:
- Use [Date Picker](/ui/docs/components/forms/date-picker) if the calendar should appear within a compact popover triggered from a form field or table toolbar.
- Use [Date Range Picker](/ui/docs/components/forms/date-picker#date-range-picker-with-presets) if you need preset ranges (such as "Last 30 days" or "This quarter") attached to a popover trigger.
- Use [Input](/ui/docs/components/forms/input) with `type="date"` only when native mobile OS date pickers are explicitly preferred over consistent cross-browser styling.

## Examples

### Single date

By default, `Calendar` runs in single-date mode (`mode="single"`). Provide `value` and `onValueChange` for controlled operation.

```tsx
'use client';

import { useState } from 'react';
import { Calendar } from '@innostes/ui';

export function DispatchDateSelector() {
  const [dispatchDate, setDispatchDate] = useState<Date | null>(new Date());

  return (
    <Calendar
      value={dispatchDate}
      onValueChange={setDispatchDate}
      aria-label="Dispatch schedule"
    />
  );
}
```

### Date range

Set `mode="range"` to allow selecting a start date and an end date. Setting `numberOfMonths={2}` renders two consecutive months side-by-side, which simplifies picking cross-month accounting or reporting cycles.

```tsx
'use client';

import { useState } from 'react';
import { Calendar, type DateRange } from '@innostes/ui';

export function AuditRangeCalendar() {
  const [range, setRange] = useState<DateRange>({
    from: new Date(2026, 3, 1),
    to: new Date(2026, 3, 15),
  });

  return (
    <Calendar
      mode="range"
      numberOfMonths={2}
      value={range}
      onValueChange={setRange}
      aria-label="Audit observation period"
    />
  );
}
```

### Date constraints and disabled dates

Pass `min` and `max` bounds to prevent selecting dates outside allowable fiscal limits. Use `isDateDisabled` to disable specific calendar dates, such as gazetted public holidays or weekend warehouse closures.

```tsx
import { Calendar } from '@innostes/ui';

const isWeekend = (date: Date) => date.getDay() === 0 || date.getDay() === 6;

export function WarehouseCutoffCalendar() {
  return (
    <Calendar
      min={new Date(2026, 0, 1)}
      max={new Date(2026, 11, 31)}
      isDateDisabled={isWeekend}
      aria-label="Warehouse loading date"
    />
  );
}
```

### Dropdown year and month navigation

For dates far in the past or future (such as incorporation dates or employee date of birth), set `captionLayout="dropdown"`. This substitutes plain month header text with accessible select dropdowns for rapid jumping.

```tsx
import { Calendar } from '@innostes/ui';

export function IncorporationCalendar() {
  return (
    <Calendar
      captionLayout="dropdown"
      fromYear={1990}
      toYear={2030}
      aria-label="Entity incorporation date"
    />
  );
}
```

### Locale and week start

Month and weekday labels automatically derive from the user's browser runtime through `Intl.DateTimeFormat`. You can pass an explicit BCP 47 locale tag (`locale="en-IN"`) or override the first day of the week with `weekStartsOn` (where `0` is Sunday and `1` is Monday).

```tsx
import { Calendar } from '@innostes/ui';

export function IndianFiscalCalendar() {
  return (
    <Calendar
      locale="en-IN"
      weekStartsOn={1}
      aria-label="GST filing schedule"
    />
  );
}
```

### Time zones

`Calendar` operates strictly on **local calendar days**:
- Values are native JavaScript `Date` instances clamped to midnight in the local browser runtime.
- The component does not apply UTC hour offsets or time zone translations.
- When sending values to an ERP API, serialise the calendar day to an ISO date string format (`YYYY-MM-DD`) at the application boundary, rather than sending a raw UTC timestamp that could shift the calendar day across midnight in eastern or western longitudes.

## Accessibility

`Calendar` implements the W3C WAI-ARIA Date Picker Grid design pattern.

### Keyboard navigation

The calendar grid is a single tab stop with roving tabindex across days.

<KeyboardTable
  entries={[
    { key: 'Left Arrow', action: 'Moves focus to the previous day.' },
    { key: 'Right Arrow', action: 'Moves focus to the next day.' },
    { key: 'Up Arrow', action: 'Moves focus to the same weekday in the previous week.' },
    { key: 'Down Arrow', action: 'Moves focus to the same weekday in the next week.' },
    { key: 'Home', action: 'Moves focus to the first day of the current week.' },
    { key: 'End', action: 'Moves focus to the last day of the current week.' },
    { key: 'Page Up', action: 'Navigates to the previous month.' },
    { key: 'Page Down', action: 'Navigates to the next month.' },
    { key: 'Shift + Page Up', action: 'Navigates to the previous calendar year.' },
    { key: 'Shift + Page Down', action: 'Navigates to the next calendar year.' },
    { key: 'Enter / Space', action: 'Selects the currently focused day.' },
  ]}
/>

### Screen readers

- The month table uses `role="grid"` with column headers denoting abbreviated and full weekday names (`abbr` attribute).
- Each cell has a full textual accessible label (e.g., "Thursday, 15 October 2026").
- The current calendar date is marked with `aria-current="date"`.
- Selected dates communicate their status through `aria-selected="true"`.
- Disabled days maintain keyboard focusability to allow navigating across weeks without breaking roving focus, marked with `aria-disabled="true"`.

## Guidelines

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Clamp dates to midnight (00:00:00) in local time when computing boundaries to avoid subtle 1-hour daylight saving or offset mismatches.',
    code: `const start = new Date(2026, 3, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0);`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not pass raw UTC timestamps from an API directly into min or max props without converting to local calendar days.',
    code: `// Can cause boundary skew across timezones\n<Calendar min={new Date('2026-04-01T00:00:00.000Z')} />`,
  }}
/>

<DoDont
  do={{
    description: 'Use `numberOfMonths={2}` when rendering range mode on desktop screens so users can inspect start and end dates spanning consecutive months.',
    code: `<Calendar mode="range" numberOfMonths={2} value={range} onValueChange={setRange} />`,
  }}
  dont={{
    description: 'Do not use multi-month layouts inside narrow mobile dialogs or sidebars where horizontal scrolling would be required.',
    code: `<div className="w-64">\n  <Calendar numberOfMonths={2} />\n</div>`,
  }}
/>

## API reference

<ApiTable components={['Calendar']} />

- [Field](/ui/docs/components/forms/field) — Accessible container with labels, descriptions, and error messages.
- [Locale Selects](/ui/docs/components/forms/locale-select) — Regional preference dropdowns for timezones, countries, and date formats.

## Checkbox (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/forms/checkbox)

Accessible checkbox primitive supporting single agreement boxes, multi-select tables, and indeterminate "select all" parent groups.

import { CheckboxPlayground } from '@/components/docs/checkbox-playground';

`Checkbox` allows users to select one or multiple items from a list, toggle optional settings, or confirm legal agreements. Built on Base UI's checkbox primitive, it supports three visual and semantic states: checked, unchecked, and indeterminate (mixed).

<ComponentPreview name="forms/checkbox/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import { Checkbox, CheckboxGroup } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

- **Use Checkbox** when users can select multiple options independently from a list, or toggle an isolated agreement (e.g. "I accept the delivery terms").
- **Use Switch** for binary options that take effect immediately without requiring form submission.
- **Use RadioGroup** when users must choose exactly one option from a mutually exclusive set.

## Examples

### Interactive playground

Experiment with checked, indeterminate, and disabled states:

<CheckboxPlayground />

### Single checkbox in a field

Wrap a checkbox inside `<Field>` with an accessible label:

```tsx
<Field>
  <label className="flex items-center gap-2.5 text-sm cursor-pointer">
    <Checkbox name="expressDelivery" />
    <span>Enable express carrier dispatch (Karnataka Hub)</span>
  </label>
  <FieldDescription>Guarantees delivery within 24 hours.</FieldDescription>
</Field>
```

### Indeterminate select all group

`CheckboxGroup` coordinates multiple child checkboxes and exposes a parent "select all" trigger that enters an indeterminate state when a partial subset of rows is selected:

<ComponentPreview name="forms/checkbox/group" />

```tsx
<CheckboxGroup
  value={selectedOrders}
  onValueChange={setSelectedOrders}
  allValues={['PO-101', 'PO-102', 'PO-103']}
>
  {({ isAllSelected, isSomeSelected, selectAll, unselectAll }) => (
    <div className="space-y-3">
      <label className="flex items-center gap-2 font-medium">
        <Checkbox
          checked={isAllSelected}
          indeterminate={isSomeSelected && !isAllSelected}
          onCheckedChange={(checked) => (checked ? selectAll() : unselectAll())}
        />
        <span>Select all purchase orders</span>
      </label>
      <div className="ms-6 space-y-2">
        <label className="flex items-center gap-2 text-sm">
          <Checkbox value="PO-101" /> PO-101 (₹45,000)
        </label>
        <label className="flex items-center gap-2 text-sm">
          <Checkbox value="PO-102" /> PO-102 (₹82,400)
        </label>
      </div>
    </div>
  )}
</CheckboxGroup>
```

## Accessibility

### Keyboard navigation

<KeyboardTable
  rows={[
    { key: 'Space', action: 'Toggles the checkbox between checked and unchecked.' },
    { key: 'Tab', action: 'Moves focus to the checkbox or moves to the next focusable element.' },
  ]}
/>

### Screen readers and ARIA

- **`role="checkbox"`**: Emits standard checkbox semantics.
- **`aria-checked`**: Sets `aria-checked="true"`, `false`, or `"mixed"` when in the indeterminate state.
- **Label coupling**: Wrapping the checkbox inside `<label>` or associating via `aria-label` ensures screen readers announce the label clearly upon focus.

## Guidelines

<DoDont>
  <Do>
    Use positive phrasing for checkbox labels (e.g. "Send shipment status notifications via SMS").
  </Do>
  <Dont>
    Never use negative phrasing such as "Do not notify me via SMS" which creates double-negative confusion.
  </Dont>
</DoDont>

<DoDont>
  <Do>
    Use the indeterminate state exclusively on parent checkboxes to indicate partial selection of a child set.
  </Do>
  <Dont>
    Never use indeterminate as an independent "maybe" or "unknown" choice for standalone user input.
  </Dont>
</DoDont>

## API reference

<ApiTable components={['Checkbox', 'CheckboxGroup']} baseUi="checkbox" />

- [Switch](/ui/docs/components/forms/switch) — Instant-acting binary switch toggle.
- [RadioGroup](/ui/docs/components/forms/radio-group) — Mutually exclusive option selection.
- [DataTable](/ui/docs/components/data-display/data-table) — High-density data grid with built-in checkbox row selection.

## Combobox (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/forms/combobox)

Accessible combobox input for filtering and selecting values from extensive or remote dataset collections.

`Combobox` combines a text input with a floating listbox popup. Built on Base UI's combobox primitive, it allows operators to type to filter large datasets, traverse options using arrow keys, and select records with keyboard or pointer input. It is designed for searching customer records, product SKUs, and general ledgers across Northwind Traders systems.

<ComponentPreview name="forms/combobox/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import {
  Combobox,
  ComboboxInput,
  ComboboxContent,
  ComboboxList,
  ComboboxItem,
  ComboboxEmpty,
  ComboboxGroup,
  ComboboxGroupLabel,
  ComboboxSeparator,
} from '@innostes/ui';
```

## When to use

- **Use Combobox** when users need to filter through extensive datasets (50 to 10,000+ items) or query remote server endpoints asynchronously.
- **Use SearchableSelect** for moderate client-side lists (15 to 100 items) where a standard select trigger is preferred.
- **Use Select** when the list of options is short (under 15 items) and typing to filter is unnecessary.
- **Use TagInput** when users select and manage multiple tags or keywords concurrently.

### Selection control comparison

| Control | Selection count | Number of options | Search filter | Best suited for |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Combobox** | Single or Multi | 50 to 10,000+ | Yes | Large async remote datasets or autocomplete with custom item creation |
| **[SearchableSelect](/ui/docs/components/forms/searchable-select)** | Single | 15 to 100+ | Yes | Moderate lists requiring fast dropdown filter search |
| **[Select](/ui/docs/components/forms/select)** | Single or Multi | 5 to 15 | No (type-ahead) | Compact predefined lists (e.g. status, payment terms) |
| **[RadioGroup](/ui/docs/components/forms/radio-group)** | Single | 2 to 5 | No | Visible choices where side-by-side comparison is essential |
| **[TagInput](/ui/docs/components/forms/tag-input)** | Multi | Variable | Yes | Categorical metadata, SKU keywords, and multi-tag filtering |

## Examples

### Object collections with custom labels

When working with complex domain objects, supply `itemToStringLabel` to tell the combobox which property represents the human-readable string:

```tsx
interface Vendor {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  gstin: string;
}

const vendors: Vendor[] = [
  { id: 'v1', name: 'Hindustan Industrial Spares', gstin: '29AAAAA0000A1Z5' },
  { id: 'v2', name: 'Bharat Electricals Ltd', gstin: '29BBBBB1111B2Z6' },
];

<Combobox items={vendors} itemToStringLabel={(v) => v.name}>
  <ComboboxInput placeholder="Search supplier organisation..." />
  <ComboboxContent>
    <ComboboxEmpty>No vendor found.</ComboboxEmpty>
    <ComboboxList>
      {(vendor: Vendor) => (
        <ComboboxItem key={vendor.id} value={vendor}>
          <div>
            <div className="font-medium">{vendor.name}</div>
            <div className="text-xs text-muted-foreground font-mono">{vendor.gstin}</div>
          </div>
        </ComboboxItem>
      )}
    </ComboboxList>
  </ComboboxContent>
</Combobox>
```

### Server-side search filtering

Control input queries using `onInputValueChange` to query remote backend endpoints with debounced network calls:

```tsx
const [query, setQuery] = useState('');
const [items, setItems] = useState<Customer[]>([]);

<Combobox
  items={items}
  onInputValueChange={(val) => {
    setQuery(val);
    fetchCustomersDebounced(val).then(setItems);
  }}
>
  <ComboboxInput placeholder="Type customer name or GSTIN..." />
  <ComboboxContent>
    <ComboboxEmpty>No records matching search query.</ComboboxEmpty>
    <ComboboxList>
      {(item) => <ComboboxItem key={item.id} value={item}>{item.name}</ComboboxItem>}
    </ComboboxList>
  </ComboboxContent>
</Combobox>
```

## Accessibility

### Keyboard navigation

<KeyboardTable
  rows={[
    { key: 'ArrowDown', action: 'Opens the listbox if closed, or highlights the subsequent option.' },
    { key: 'ArrowUp', action: 'Highlights the preceding option, or closes the popup when at the top.' },
    { key: 'Enter', action: 'Selects the currently highlighted option and closes the listbox.' },
    { key: 'Escape', action: 'Dismisses the listbox popup without changing the selected value.' },
  ]}
/>

### Screen readers and ARIA

- **WAI-ARIA Combobox pattern**: The `<ComboboxInput>` acts as `role="combobox"` linked to the floating `<ComboboxContent>` which acts as `role="listbox"`.
- **`aria-activedescendant`**: Updated dynamically as keyboard arrows cycle highlighted items so screen readers announce each option without shifting native DOM focus from the text input.

## Guidelines

<DoDont>
  <Do>
    Provide an informative `<ComboboxEmpty>` state informing the user when no search results match.
  </Do>
  <Dont>
    Never show an empty, blank floating container when a search yields zero matches.
  </Dont>
</DoDont>

<DoDont>
  <Do>
    Use debounced asynchronous fetching when searching massive datasets over the network.
  </Do>
  <Dont>
    Never trigger an unthrottled HTTP request on every individual keystroke.
  </Dont>
</DoDont>

## API reference

<ApiTable
  components={[
    'Combobox',
    'ComboboxInput',
    'ComboboxContent',
    'ComboboxList',
    'ComboboxItem',
    'ComboboxEmpty',
    'ComboboxGroup',
    'ComboboxGroupLabel',
    'ComboboxSeparator',
  ]}
  baseUi="combobox"
/>

## Related

- [SearchableSelect](/ui/docs/components/forms/searchable-select) — Filterable dropdown menu for medium option lists.
- [Select](/ui/docs/components/forms/select) — Standard dropdown select for short, static option lists.
- [TagInput](/ui/docs/components/forms/tag-input) — Multi-tag entry and keyword selection.
